definition_zh: 输入；投入（资源、意见）；输入端；输入数据
definition_en: something put into a system, such as data, effort, or money, or the act of putting it in
core_image: 一只手把数据卡片推进机器的进料口
scene: 技术员坐在电脑前核对屏幕上的一行行数字。 The new software needs less input from the user.
sceneCN: 这里 input 是「输入」（第 1 个义项：输入系统的数据或指令）；句意为新软件需要的用户输入更少。图中可辨识物件：键盘、屏幕、数据卡。

pos.zh: 名词：输入；投入；输入端；输入数据

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 device 构成，义为「输入设备」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「数据录入」
由前缀 out- 构成的对应词，义为「输出」

senses.title: Data put into a computer
senses.definition: information or instructions put into a computer or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 送入计算机或机器的信息或指令
senses.example: The program waits for input from the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 程序等待来自键盘的输入。
senses.why: Input is the noun of putting in: whatever is pushed into a system through its entrance.
senses.whyCN: input 是「put in」的名词：凡经入口推送进系统的东西。

senses.title: Effort or resources put in
senses.definition: the effort, money, advice, or time given to a project, often by several people
senses.definitionCN: 投入某项工程的努力、资金、建议或时间，常由多方提供
senses.example: The report was written with input from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是在各部门的意见基础上写成的。
senses.why: Factories speak of inputs of labour and materials, and meetings of inputs of advice.
senses.whyCN: 工厂说劳动与材料的投入，会议说建议的投入。

senses.title: The terminal that receives data
senses.definition: a place or device through which signals enter a system
senses.definitionCN: 信号进入系统的位置或装置
senses.example: Plug the cable into the audio input.
senses.exampleCN: 把线插进音频输入口。
senses.why: The entrance point takes the name of what passes through it.
senses.whyCN: 入口处往往就以流经它的东西命名。

intro.en: Input is not Latin at all: it is put with the prefix in- on the English model of output.
intro.cn: input 完全不是拉丁词：它是英语把 put 加前缀 in- 造出的词，与 output 对应。

items.en: Put has no certain origin even in Old English, where it appears in place names.
items.cn: put 连在古英语中也来源不明，只在地名里出现。

items.en: Input was formed in the eighteenth century for money and resources put into a business.
items.cn: input 在十八世纪造出，指投入企业的资金与资源。

items.en: Engineers took up the word for power and signals feeding a machine.
items.cn: 十九世纪工程师用它指供给机器的动力与信号。

items.en: Computing fixed the sense of data entered into a system, and output grew beside it.
items.cn: 计算机业固定了「输入数据」的义项，output 随之而来。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to advice and effort contributed by people.
items.cn: 日常用语又把它扩展到人们贡献的意见与努力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words made with put and with the prefix in-; the near-meaning group gathers other words for contributions.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 与 in- 构成的词；近义组收表示「贡献」的其他词。

entries.definition: What a system produces, the opposite of input.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输出」，与 input 相对。

entries.definition: The act of entering data.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据录入」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, with a Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进口」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Something given to a shared effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献」，指对共同努力的付出。

entries.definition: Information in a form a computer can process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据」，指可供计算机处理的信息。

entries.definition: Money or effort put in for future gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投资」，指为将来收益而投入的钱或力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain English build of the word, which is simply in plus put.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用这个词朴素的英语构成，即 in 加 put。

normal.en: Input is in plus put: what you put in.
normal.cn: input 就是 in 加 put：你投入进去的东西。

normal.en: Output sits on the other side of the same wall.
normal.cn: output 位于同一堵墙的另一侧。

normal.en: Ask for input before you write the report, not after.
normal.cn: 写报告之前征求意见，别等后面。

normal.en: Users type input; the computer answers with output.
normal.cn: 用户键入 input，计算机回以 output。

normal.en: An audio input is the socket that lets sound in.
normal.cn: audio input 是让声音进来的插孔。

abstract.en: Picture grain poured into a hopper: what goes in determines what comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象谷物倒进料斗：送进去的决定了出来的。

abstract.en: A system is only as good as the input it receives.
abstract.cn: 系统的质量取决于它接收的输入。

abstract.en: Every effort you put in is a kind of input, even when nobody records it.
abstract.cn: 你的每一点付出都是一种输入，即使没人记录。

examples.en: The form asks for input of your personal details.
examples.cn: 表格要求输入你的个人信息。

examples.en: We would welcome input from parents on the new timetable.
examples.cn: 新课程表方面我们欢迎家长提出意见。

examples.en: Insert the microphone into the input at the back.
examples.cn: 把麦克风插到后面的输入口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因普特」——因「普特」把数据输入了电脑

root: input 是英语用 in- + put 仿 output 构成的词，十八世纪指投入企业的资金与资源；十九世纪用于机器动力与信号，二十世纪计算机业固定为「数据输入」，后引申为「意见投入」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: data entering a machine, resources or advice entering a project, and the socket where signals enter.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：进入机器的数据、进入项目的资源与意见，以及信号进入的接口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain is poured into a hopper; what goes in decides what comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷物倒进料斗，进多少决定出多少。

branches.en: THE KEYBOARD: typing is the commonest form of input.
branches.cn: 键盘这条线：打字是最常见的 input。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a program cannot run without data from somewhere.
branches.cn: 程序这条线：没有数据来源，程序无法运行。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a good decision needs input from the people affected.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：好的决定需要受影响者的意见。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: labour, fuel and material are the inputs of production.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：劳动、燃料与材料是生产的投入。

branches.en: THE SOCKET: the input is also the physical entrance.
branches.cn: 接口这条线：the input 也指物理上的入口。

intro.en: Input is a modern English compound; the prefix in- carries the sense of entering.
intro.cn: input 是现代英语复合词，前缀 in- 承载「进入」之意。

latinIntro.en: The form looks Latin but is English; the table records the native and Latin-related elements honestly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词形似拉丁语，其实是英语词；下表如实区分本族要素与相关拉丁要素。

items.example: It marks the direction of the putting.
A verb of uncertain origin, recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已有记录的动词，来源不确定。

items.example: It has no separate meaning now.
The partner word on the other side.
It forms inputted in some uses.
The same prefix in Latin words such as inject.
items.exampleCN: 在 inject 等拉丁词中也有同一前缀。

definition_zh: 遍及；贯穿整个；自始至终
definition_en: in every part of a place or thing, or during the whole of a period of time
core_image: 一盏灯从屋顶照下来，屋里每个角落都被照亮
scene: 这座城市从南到北都在下雨,骑车的人个个罩着雨衣。 Rain fell throughout the city, from the harbour to the northern hills.
sceneCN: 这里 throughout 是「遍及、贯穿整个」（第 1 个义项：空间上的每一处）；句意为整座城市从港口到北边山地都在下雨。

forms.label: 无变化（介词与副词同形）

derivatives.zh: 复合中的前一部分，义为「穿过」
复合中的后一部分，义为「向外、全部」
同根孪生词，义为「彻底的」

senses.title: In every part of a place
senses.definition: in or into every part of a place, area or object
senses.definitionCN: 在某地、某区域或某物体的每一部分中
senses.example: The fire alarm could be heard throughout the building.
senses.exampleCN: 整栋楼都能听见火警铃声。
senses.why: Through supplies the passage and out supplies the spread, so the word covers every part of a space.
senses.whyCN: through 提供「贯穿」，out 提供「铺开」，于是这个词覆盖了一个空间的每一部分。

senses.title: During the whole of a period
senses.titleCN: 自始至终；贯穿整个时期
senses.definition: during the whole of a period of time, from beginning to end
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间的整个过程中，从头到尾
senses.example: She remained calm throughout the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 整个面试过程中她都保持镇定。
senses.why: Time is crossed the same way a space is: the compound reaches both ends of the period.
senses.whyCN: 时间与空间以同样的方式被穿过：这个复合词抵达这段时间的两端。

senses.title: In all parts of a group or field
senses.definition: in every part of a group, field or body of work
senses.definitionCN: 在某个群体、领域或全部作品中的每一处
senses.example: The idea appears throughout his early novels.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法贯穿他早期的小说。
senses.why: A body of work is treated like a place, and the idea is found in every part of it.
senses.whyCN: 一批作品被当作一个地方，而这个想法在其中每一处都能找到。

senses.title: As a standalone adverb
senses.definition: used alone, especially after a noun, to mean in every part or the whole time
senses.definitionCN: 单独作副词，尤用于名词之后，表示「处处」或「一直」
senses.example: The house was painted white throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子里里外外都刷成了白色。
senses.why: With no noun after it, the compound simply means all over, in space or in time.
senses.whyCN: 后面不接名词时，这个复合词就单纯表示「到处、始终」，用于空间或时间。

intro.en: Throughout is a plain English compound of through and out, first recorded in the Old English period.
intro.cn: throughout 是 through 与 out 构成的朴实英语复合词，最早见于古英语时期。

items.en: The compound of þurh and ūt already meant on every side or entirely, built the same way as other out compounds.
items.cn: þurh 与 ūt 的复合在古英语已表示「四面八方、完全」，与其他带 out 的复合词构词相同。

items.en: Middle English throughout kept both the spatial sense and the temporal one, and settled as a single word.
items.cn: 中古英语 throughout 兼有空间与时间两义，并固定为一个词。

items.en: Early modern English added the extended use for groups and works, as in throughout his writings.
items.cn: 早期现代英语增添了用于群体与作品的引申用法，如 throughout his writings。

items.en: Modern English uses throughout more in writing than in speech, where all through is often preferred.
items.cn: 现代英语里 throughout 多用于书面，口语更常用 all through。

items.en: The adverb use without a following noun remains common, as in painted white throughout.
items.cn: 不接名词的副词用法依然常见，如 painted white throughout。

note.en: The first group unpacks the compound and its relatives; the second compares prepositions of extent.
note.cn: 第一组拆解这个复合词及其亲属；第二组比较表示范围的介词。

entries.definition: From one side to the other; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过；复合词的前半

entries.definition: The everyday spoken equivalent, common before a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 口语常用说法，多接时间段

entries.definition: Complete and careful; the adjective twin of through.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的（through 的形容词孪生词）

entries.definition: Covering every part of a place; the loose spoken partner of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 遍布；本词的口语松散对应说法

entries.definition: In every place; it cannot take a noun after it.
entries.definitionCN: 到处（后不能接名词）

entries.definition: Covering the whole of a surface or place, often informally.
entries.definitionCN: 遍布（多用于口语）

entries.definition: From one side to the other, or over the whole of an area.
entries.definitionCN: 横跨；遍及

entries.definition: Through the course of a period; it does not mean everywhere in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在……期间（不含空间「遍及」义）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the two parts of the compound and from its written register.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自复合词的两个部分，以及它的书面语体。

normal.en: Throughout is through plus out: passing through, then spread out everywhere.
normal.cn: throughout 就是 through 加 out：先穿过，再铺开到各处。

normal.en: Use it for places and for periods, but not for a point in time.
normal.cn: 它用于地点与时段，不用于某个时间点。

normal.en: In speech, all through often does the same job.
normal.cn: 口语里 all through 常干同样的活。

normal.en: The adverb use takes no noun: white throughout means white all over.
normal.cn: 副词用法不接名词：white throughout 意为里外全白。

normal.en: Mind the noun after it: throughout the city, not throughout city.
normal.cn: 注意后面要有冠词或限定词：throughout the city。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp hung from the ceiling, reaching the corners the floor lamp misses.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏吊灯挂在天花板上，照到了落地灯照不到的角落。

abstract.en: The word stretches a space or a period until nothing outside it remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词把一个空间或一段时间拉长，直到外面什么都不剩。

abstract.en: It is the quiet, written cousin of everywhere.
abstract.cn: 它是 everywhere 那个安静的书面对应词。

examples.en: The festival is celebrated throughout the country.
examples.cn: 这个节日在全国各地都庆祝。

examples.en: He kept notes throughout the lecture.
examples.cn: 整场讲座他都在记笔记。

examples.en: The walls were painted pale grey throughout.
examples.cn: 墙里里外外都刷成了浅灰色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出路熬特」——出路熬到特别久，一路贯彻到底 → throughout 自始至终

root: 古英语由 þurh（through，穿过）+ ūt（out，向外）复合而成，表示「四面八方、完全」，后兼指时间自始至终，并引申用于群体与作品。

sensesIntro.en: Throughout stretches the tunnel image over a space, a period, a body of work, or the whole of an object.
sensesIntro.cn: throughout 把隧道意象拉伸到一片空间、一段时间、一批作品，或一个物体的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp hung high, lighting every corner at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：高悬的灯，一次照亮每个角落。

branches.en: The space: every room, every region.
branches.cn: 空间线：每间屋、每个地区。

branches.en: The period: from beginning to end.
branches.cn: 时段线：从开头到结尾。

branches.en: The field: across a whole body of ideas or novels.
branches.cn: 领域线：贯穿全部想法或小说。

branches.en: The object: white throughout, without a noun.
branches.cn: 物体线：white throughout，不带名词。

branches.en: Place and time are stretched by the same compound.
branches.cn: 空间与时间由同一个复合词拉满。

intro.en: Throughout is itself a compound; it does not take further endings.
intro.cn: throughout 本身已是复合词，不再加其他词尾。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都是英语本土词，拉丁词条留空。

definition_zh: 信封；封套；外膜；极限
definition_en: a paper cover for a letter, or any enclosing cover
core_image: 一张纸把信折包在里面，只露出封口
scene: 她把照片放进棕色信封，写上地址。 She put the photo in a brown envelope and wrote the address.
sceneCN: 这里 envelope 是「信封」（第 1 个义项：装信件或文件的纸套）；句意：她把照片装进棕色信封并写上地址。

derivatives.zh: 包住；裹住
包裹；包围

senses.title: A paper cover for a letter
senses.definition: a flat paper container used for sending letters or papers
senses.definitionCN: 用于寄送信件或文件的扁平纸制容器
senses.example: He sealed the envelope and mailed it.
senses.exampleCN: 他把信封封好并寄了出去。
senses.why: The word comes from a French verb meaning to wrap, so the paper wrapper for a letter is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自意为「包裹」的法语动词，所以装信件的纸套是它的第一个义项。

senses.title: Any enclosing cover
senses.definition: a layer or cover that wraps something around
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从四周包起来的层或罩
senses.example: A thin envelope of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子上覆着一层薄薄的灰尘。
senses.why: The idea of wrapping extends from paper to any surrounding layer.
senses.whyCN: 「包裹」的概念从纸张扩展到任何包围的层。

senses.title: The limit of what is accepted
senses.definition: the boundary of what is normal or possible, especially in performance
senses.definitionCN: 正常或可能范围的边界，尤指表现方面
senses.example: The test pilots pushed the envelope of speed.
senses.exampleCN: 试飞员挑战了速度的极限。
senses.why: Aircraft have a safe operating envelope, and pushing beyond it became a general image for testing limits.
senses.whyCN: 飞机有安全运行包线，越过它就成了一般意义上「挑战极限」的意象。

senses.title: A technical outer membrane
senses.definition: a membrane or outer layer enclosing a cell, virus, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 包住细胞、病毒或结构的膜或外层
senses.example: The virus is wrapped in a protein envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒外面包着一层蛋白质外膜。
senses.why: The biological sense applies the same enclosing idea at a microscopic scale.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义项把同样的包裹概念用于微观尺度。

intro.en: Envelope comes from Old French envoloper, to wrap, which goes back to Latin volvere, to roll or turn.
intro.cn: envelope 来自古法语 envoloper（包裹），其根源是拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll or turn around.
items.cn: volvere 意为卷动或转动。

items.en: Voloper develops the sense of wrapping.
items.cn: voloper 发展出「包裹」的含义。

items.en: Envoloper means to wrap something up.
items.cn: envoloper 意为把某物包起来。

items.en: Enveloppe names the wrapper itself.
items.cn: enveloppe 指包裹物本身。

items.en: English envelope first means a wrapper and then a letter cover.
items.cn: 英语 envelope 先指包裹物，再指信封。

items.en: Modern English adds the technical senses of limit and membrane.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「极限」与「外膜」等技术义项。

note.en: Envelope is a wrapping noun, closely tied to the verb envelop and to words for covers.
note.cn: envelope 是表示包裹的名词，与动词 envelop 以及表示覆盖的词关系紧密。

entries.definition: to wrap or surround completely
entries.definitionCN: 包住；包围

entries.definition: the act of wrapping or surrounding
entries.definitionCN: 包裹；包围

entries.definition: surrounding on all sides
entries.definitionCN: 四面围住的

entries.definition: a cover around something
entries.definitionCN: 包装纸；封套

entries.definition: a thing placed over another
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖物；封面

entries.definition: an outer protective shell
entries.definitionCN: 外壳；套管

normalIntro.en: Envelope is the noun of envelop: it is the thing that wraps a letter and holds it inside.
normalIntro.cn: envelope 是 envelop 的名词：它就是包住信件、把信装在里面的事物。

normal.en: A sealed envelope hides the letter until it is opened.
normal.cn: 封好的信封把信藏起来，直到被打开。

normal.en: To push the envelope is to test a limit.
normal.cn: push the envelope 就是挑战极限。

normal.en: The verb envelop means to wrap, with no final e sound.
normal.cn: 动词 envelop 意为包裹，结尾不读长音。

normal.en: A biological envelope is an outer membrane.
normal.cn: 生物学中的 envelope 是外膜。

normal.en: Compare wrapper: wrapper is general, envelope is usually paper for mail.
normal.cn: 对比 wrapper：wrapper 更泛指包装，envelope 通常指邮寄用的纸套。

abstract.en: Picture two paper flaps folding over a sealed letter.
abstract.cn: 想象两片纸翼折过来盖住一封封好的信。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin ring of dust around a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象灯周围有一圈薄薄的灰尘。

abstract.en: Think of a plane flying at the edge of its safe range.
abstract.cn: 想象一架飞机飞在安全范围的边缘。

examples.en: She licked the envelope and pressed it shut.
examples.cn: 她舔了舔信封，把它压紧封好。

examples.en: A soft envelope of mist lay over the field.
examples.cn: 田野上覆着一层柔和的薄雾。

examples.en: Engineers keep testing the envelope of the new design.
examples.cn: 工程师们不断测试新设计的性能极限。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「en + velope」——把信「包」进纸里，就成信封；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（卷、转）→ 古法语 envoloper（包裹）→ enveloppe（包裹物）→ 英语 envelope，核心义「包在外面的套子」。

sensesIntro.en: Envelope starts as a paper wrapper, extends to any enclosing layer, then to a boundary of performance and a biological membrane.
sensesIntro.cn: envelope 从纸信封开始，扩展到任何包围层，再扩展到性能界限与生物外膜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: paper folded around a letter, sealed on all sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸从四面折起包住一封信并封好。

branches.en: The mail cover is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 邮寄用的纸套是日常义项。

branches.en: Any enclosing layer extends the wrap idea.
branches.cn: 任何包围层都扩展了「包裹」的概念。

branches.en: The safe operating range became an image for limits.
branches.cn: 安全运行包线成为「极限」的意象。

branches.en: The biological membrane applies the outer-layer sense.
branches.cn: 生物外膜运用了「外层」义项。

branches.en: Both a letter cover and a dust layer enclose something.
branches.cn: 信封与灰尘层都把某物包在里面。

intro.en: Envelope belongs to the volvere family of wrapping words, with the verb envelop and the noun envelopment.
intro.cn: envelope 属于 volvere 这一「包裹」词族，另有动词 envelop 与名词 envelopment。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere means to roll, and involvere means to wrap around.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为卷动，involvere 意为缠绕包裹。

items.example: Involvere adds the sense of enclosing.
Envoloper is the French wrapping verb.
items.exampleCN: envoloper 是法语中表示包裹的动词。

definition_zh: 羞愧的；惭愧的；不好意思的；不愿承认的
definition_en: feeling shame or embarrassment about one's own actions, about a situation, or about admitting something
core_image: 低着头、脸发烫，恨不得躲到桌子底下
scene: 教室后排的男孩低着头，手指绞着衣角，不敢看讲台上的老师。 He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
sceneCN: 这里 ashamed 是「羞愧的」（第 1 个义项：因自己的行为而感到羞耻）；句意为「他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧」。画面中有教室后排、低头的男孩与绞着衣角的手。

pos.zh: 形容词：羞愧的；惭愧的；不好意思的；不愿承认的

derivatives.zh: ashamed 的词根名词，义为「羞耻；羞愧；憾事」
由 shame 加 -ful 构成，义为「可耻的；丢脸的」
由 shame 加 -less 构成，义为「无耻的；不知羞耻的」

senses.title: Feeling shame for one's own act
senses.definition: feeling shame or guilt because of something one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因自己做过的事而感到羞耻或内疚
senses.example: He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧。
senses.why: The word is a past participle, as if shame had been poured over the person and left him covered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是过去分词，好像羞耻被浇在这个人身上，让他浑身都罩着它。

senses.title: Embarrassed by a situation
senses.definition: feeling embarrassed about a situation, especially one caused by others or by one's family
senses.definitionCN: 因某种处境、尤指由他人或家人造成的处境而感到难堪
senses.example: She was ashamed of her family's noisy quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 她为家里那场吵闹的争吵感到难堪。
senses.why: Shame does not need to be earned: whatever places you in the wrong light can cover you too.
senses.whyCN: 羞耻不必是自己挣来的：任何把你放到不光彩位置的事，都能把羞耻罩到你身上。

senses.title: Unwilling to admit something
senses.definition: reluctant to admit or reveal something because it feels humiliating
senses.definitionCN: 因觉得丢脸而不愿承认或透露某事
senses.example: He was ashamed to admit that he had failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他不好意思承认自己失败了。
senses.why: To admit is to stand uncovered before others, and the ashamed person refuses that exposure.
senses.whyCN: 承认就是把自己毫无遮掩地站到人前，而羞愧的人拒绝这种暴露。

intro.en: Ashamed is literally 'shamed', a past participle built on the Old English word for shame.
intro.cn: ashamed 字面就是「被羞耻覆盖的」，是建立在古英语「羞耻」一词上的过去分词。

items.en: 「*skamō」 meant 'shame, disgrace' and is the common source of the Germanic shame words.
items.cn: 「*skamō」意为「羞耻、丢脸」，是各日耳曼语中「羞耻」词的共同来源。

items.en: Scamu meant 'shame, modesty', and the verb scamian meant 'to feel shame'.
items.cn: scamu 意为「羞耻、羞怯」，动词 scamian 意为「感到羞耻」。

items.en: The noun became shame, and a derived verb ashame meant 'to make ashamed'.
items.cn: 名词演变为 shame，又派生出一个动词 ashame，意为「使羞愧」。

items.en: The past participle ashamed outlived the verb and became an adjective in its own right.
items.cn: 过去分词 ashamed 比动词活得更久，本身变成了形容词。

items.en: The modern word covers guilt over one's acts, embarrassment at circumstances, and reluctance to admit.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖对自己行为的愧疚、对处境的难堪，以及不愿承认。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same shame root; the near-meaning group gathers feelings of embarrassment and guilt.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「羞耻」词根上的词；近义组收难堪与愧疚一类的感受。

entries.definition: The painful feeling of having done something wrong or foolish.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「羞耻、羞愧」，因做错事或做了蠢事而痛苦的感觉。

entries.definition: Deserving shame or disgrace.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可耻的、丢脸的」。

entries.definition: Pale grey, like ash, often from shock or illness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灰白的」，常因震惊或疾病而脸色发灰。

entries.definition: Feeling awkward and self-conscious in front of others.
entries.definitionCN: 在他人面前感到难堪、不自在。

entries.definition: Feeling responsible for wrongdoing.
entries.definitionCN: 因做错事而感到负有责任。

entries.definition: Made to feel foolish or powerless in public.
entries.definitionCN: 在众人面前被弄得愚蠢或无力。

entries.definition: Extremely embarrassed or ashamed.
entries.definitionCN: 极度难堪或羞愧的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a bowed head to a family quarrel and a refusal to admit.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从低下的头，走到家里的争吵与不愿承认。

normal.en: Ashamed: the face is hot and the eyes drop.
normal.cn: ashamed：脸发烫，眼睛往下掉。

normal.en: Ashamed of a lie: the act is yours.
normal.cn: 为谎言羞愧：那件事是你做的。

normal.en: Ashamed of a quarrel: the scene is not yours, but it covers you.
normal.cn: 为争吵难堪：场面不是你造成的，却罩住了你。

normal.en: Ashamed to admit: standing uncovered is too much.
normal.cn: 不好意思承认：毫无遮掩地站着太难了。

normal.en: Shame is poured over the person like water.
normal.cn: 羞耻像水一样浇在这个人身上。

abstract.en: Shame can come from your own act or from your surroundings.
abstract.cn: 羞耻可以来自自己的行为，也可以来自周围的环境。

abstract.en: Admitting something feels like being seen without cover.
abstract.cn: 承认某事就像被人看见自己毫无遮掩。

abstract.en: The word is a state, not a deed.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一种状态，不是一个动作。

examples.en: He felt ashamed of lying to his best friend.
examples.cn: 他因对最好的朋友撒谎而感到羞愧。

examples.en: She was ashamed of her family's noisy quarrel.
examples.cn: 她为家里那场吵闹的争吵感到难堪。

examples.en: He was ashamed to admit that he had failed.
examples.cn: 他不好意思承认自己失败了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，羞的」——他低下头小声说「啊，羞的」：羞愧的

root: ashamed 字面就是「被羞耻覆盖的」：古英语 scamu 意为「羞耻」，动词 scamian 意为「感到羞耻」，中古英语里名词变成 shame，又派生动词 ashame「使羞愧」。它的过去分词 ashamed 活过了动词，独立成形容词。于是它既能指对自己的行为感到羞愧，也能指因处境或他人而难堪，还指因觉得丢脸而不愿承认。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share the state of being covered by shame: shame for one's own act, embarrassment at a situation, and reluctance to admit.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共享「被羞耻罩住」这一状态：为自己的行为羞愧、因处境难堪，以及不愿承认。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a head bowed low, a hot face, a wish to hide under the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：低低的头、发烫的脸，恨不得躲到桌子底下。

branches.en: THE OWN-ACT LINE: shame earned by what one has done.
branches.cn: 己过线：因自己做过的事而挣来的羞耻。

branches.en: THE GAZE LINE: shame brought on by a scene one did not cause.
branches.cn: 目光线：羞耻来自并非自己造成的场面。

branches.en: THE ADMISSION LINE: saying it aloud would leave one uncovered.
branches.cn: 承认线：说出口就等于让自己毫无遮掩。

branches.en: THE HONESTY LINE: a private fault and a public admission pull the same way.
branches.cn: 诚实线：私下的过失与公开的承认，拉的是同一根绳。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL LINE: both the family scene and the refused admission are about being seen.
branches.cn: 社交线：家里的场面与拒绝承认，都关乎「被看见」。

intro.en: Ashamed is a past participle turned adjective; its family is built on the noun shame plus -ful and -less.
intro.cn: ashamed 是过去分词转成的形容词，词族建立在名词 shame 加 -ful 与 -less 上。

latinIntro.en: Shame is a native Germanic word, so there is no Latin family here.
latinIntro.cn: shame 是本土日耳曼词，因此这里没有拉丁词族。

items.example: He was ashamed of his harsh words.
items.exampleCN: 他因自己刻薄的话而羞愧。

items.meaning: the feeling or condition of disgrace
items.example: She hung her head in shame.
It was a shameful way to treat a guest.
items.exampleCN: 那样对待客人真是丢脸。

items.example: The shameless lie fooled no one.
items.exampleCN: 那个无耻的谎言骗不了任何人。

items.example: The shamed official resigned at once.
items.exampleCN: 那位蒙羞的官员立刻辞职了。

items.example: He smiled ashamedly and said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 他羞愧地笑了笑，什么也没说。

items.example: She was unashamed of her accent.
items.exampleCN: 她对自己的口音毫不羞愧。

items.example: The boy gave a shamefaced nod.
items.exampleCN: 男孩面带愧色地点了点头。

definition_zh: 保险；保险费；保险业；保障
definition_en: an arrangement in which a company pays for loss or damage in return for regular payments, or the money paid for it
core_image: 一张纸写着「出事由我赔」，旁边是一摞按月交钱的小票
scene: 柜台上放着一份厚厚的保单，客户在末尾签下了名字。 She pays a small sum each month for travel insurance.
sceneCN: 这里 insurance 是「保险」（第 1 个义项：花钱买一份出事后可索赔的保障），句意为她每月交一笔小钱买旅行保险。画面里的物件：保单、签名笔、缴费小票。

pos.zh: 名词：保险；保险费；保险业；保障

derivatives.zh: 由本词去尾构成，义为「给……保险；确保」
由 insure 加 -er 构成，义为「保险公司；承保人」
由 insure 加 -ed 构成，义为「已投保的」
由 insure 加 -able 构成，义为「可保险的」

senses.title: Cover against loss
senses.definition: an agreement in which a company promises to pay you if you suffer loss, damage, or injury
senses.definitionCN: 一种约定：一旦你遭受损失、损坏或伤害，公司承诺向你赔付
senses.example: My grandfather has kept the same insurance on his house for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖父那栋房子的保险三十年没换过。
senses.why: Latin securus means "free from care"; insurance is the promise that someone will take care of the loss.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 securus 意为「无忧」，insurance 就是有人会替你承担损失的那句承诺。

senses.title: The money you pay
senses.definition: the regular sum of money paid to a company so that the agreement stays in force
senses.definitionCN: 为使约定持续有效而定期交给公司的一笔钱
senses.example: The insurance on the old van costs more than the van is worth.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧货车的保险费比车本身还值钱。
senses.why: In everyday speech the abstract promise and the money paid for it share one word.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，抽象的那份承诺和为它付的钱共用同一个词。

senses.title: The business itself
senses.definition: the industry or practice of selling this kind of protection
senses.definitionCN: 出售这类保障的行业或做法
senses.example: Insurance is one of the biggest employers in that city.
senses.exampleCN: 保险业是那座城市最大的雇主之一。
senses.why: From a single policy the word widened to name the whole trade built on policies.
senses.whyCN: 从一张保单出发，这个词扩展成了建立在保单之上的整个行业。

senses.title: A safeguard in general
senses.definition: anything that protects you or makes a bad outcome less likely
senses.definitionCN: 任何能保护你、或使坏结果不易发生的事物
senses.example: Saving money is the best insurance against a sudden job loss.
senses.exampleCN: 存钱是应对突然失业的最好保障。
senses.why: The figurative use moves from paperwork to life: whatever cushions a shock works like insurance.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法从纸面文件转到生活中：任何能缓冲冲击的东西都像保险一样起作用。

intro.en: Insurance grew out of the Latin adjective securus through French; the ending shifted in English to suit the trade.
intro.cn: insurance 源自拉丁语形容词 securus，经法语进入英语，词尾在英语里为适应这个行业而发生了变化。

items.en: The adjective securus, from se- "without" and cura "care", meant "free from care".
items.cn: 形容词 securus 由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」合成，义为「无忧的」。

items.en: Medieval merchants used securitas for the merchant guarantee behind a sea loan.
items.cn: 中世纪商人用 securitas 指海上借贷背后的商业担保。

items.en: Old French ensured the word as enseurance, meaning a promise to make someone safe.
items.cn: 古法语把它定型为 enseurance，意为「使人安全的承诺」。

items.en: English merchants of the sixteenth century used assurance for sea trade; insurance replaced it for the business of paying against risk.
items.cn: 十六世纪的英国商人用 assurance 指海上贸易；insurance 后来接替它表示对风险赔付的行业。

items.en: In the nineteenth century insurance broadened from ships to houses, health, and finally to any safeguard in speech.
items.cn: 十九世纪 insurance 从船舶扩展到房屋、健康，最后在日常言语中泛指任何保障。

note.en: The look-alike group hangs on the same Latin root of care and safety; the near-meaning group holds other words for protection.
note.cn: 形近组都挂在「忧虑、安全」这个拉丁词根上；近义组收其他表示保护的词。

entries.definition: A firm promise; in British English also a kind of life cover.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保证」，英式英语中也指某类人寿保险。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to arrange cover or to make certain.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投保；确保」。

entries.definition: Safe, or to fasten and make safe.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「安全的」，动词义为「使牢固、弄稳」。

entries.definition: The written contract of an insurance arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保单」，即保险的书面合同。

entries.definition: The fixed amount paid regularly for cover.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保险费」，即定期缴纳的固定金额。

entries.definition: The general state of being kept safe, wider than any contract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保护」，比合同意义上的保险更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks attach to the idea of care and the phrases insurance really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子围绕「忧虑、照看」这个念头，并挂上 insurance 的真实搭配。

normal.en: in- plus sur- means "into the sure": you buy your way into safety.
normal.cn: in- 加 sur- 是「进入保险状态」：花钱买进安全里。

normal.en: The same family gives insure, assured and secure.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 insure、assured、secure。

normal.en: An insurance company sells promises, not goods.
normal.cn: 保险公司卖的是承诺，而不是货物。

normal.en: Health insurance is the first thing a family budgets for.
normal.cn: 健康保险是一个家庭预算里最先安排的一项。

normal.en: Saving is insurance against the unexpected.
normal.cn: 储蓄是对意外的一种保险。

abstract.en: Insurance is a crowd sharing one person's bad day.
abstract.cn: 保险是一群人共同分担一个人的倒霉日子。

abstract.en: A policy is paper that turns into money only when things go wrong.
abstract.cn: 保单是一张只在出事时才变成钱的纸。

abstract.en: The word means care removed: someone else now carries the worry.
abstract.cn: 这个词的意思是「忧虑被移走」：如今别人替你担着那份心。

examples.en: The repair bill was far less painful because of his insurance.
examples.cn: 因为有保险，那笔修理费让人轻松多了。

examples.en: Insurance for the whole family rose again this year.
examples.cn: 全家的保险费今年又涨了。

examples.en: She treats a full pantry as insurance against hard times.
examples.cn: 她把塞满的储物柜当作应对艰难时日的保障。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阴输瑞思」——阴天输了也不慌，因为有保险

root: 拉丁语 cura「忧虑」→ securus「无忧的」→ 中世纪拉丁语 securitas「担保」→ 古法语 enseurance → 英语 insurance。同族词还有 insure、assurance、secure。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the promise of cover, the money paid for it, the trade that sells it, and any safeguard in ordinary life.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：赔付的承诺、为此付的钱、出售它的行业，以及生活中任何形式的保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signed promise that a loss will be paid for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张签好的承诺，保证损失会有人赔付。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: the company promises to pay when loss happens.
branches.cn: 合同这条线：公司承诺出事就赔。

branches.en: THE PREMIUM: the money handed over keeps the promise alive.
branches.cn: 保费这条线：交出去的钱让承诺继续有效。

branches.en: THE TRADE: a whole industry lives on selling such promises.
branches.cn: 行业这条线：整个产业靠出售这类承诺生存。

branches.en: THE SAVINGS JAR: anything that softens a shock acts as insurance.
branches.cn: 存钱罐这条线：任何能缓冲冲击的东西都起到保险作用。

branches.en: THE LINK: promise and payment are two sides of the same policy.
branches.cn: 连接线：承诺与付款是同一张保单的两面。

intro.en: Insurance splits into the negative prefix in-, the root secur- "care-free", and the noun ending -ance.
intro.cn: insurance 可拆为否定前缀 in-、词根 secur-「无忧」与名词词尾 -ance。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura and securus are well attested; only the deepest Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 与 securus 均有记载，只有最深层的印欧语形式属于重构。

items.example: It marks entry into a safe state.
items.exampleCN: 它标出进入安全状态的动作。

items.example: The root also lives in secure and security.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 secure 与 security。

items.example: The noun is the oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是这一词族最古老的成员。

items.example: The adjective joins se- with cura.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词由 se- 与 cura 合成。

items.example: Medieval use shifted it towards a guarantee.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪用法使它转向「担保」。

items.example: It turns the stem into an abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把词干变成抽象名词。

items.example: The verb was borrowed from Old French.
The suffix names the one who acts.
items.exampleCN: 后缀标出动作的施行者。

definition_zh: 询问；打听；调查
definition_en: a question you ask to get information, or an official investigation
core_image: 一张写着问题的小纸条被递进窗口，里面的人开始翻资料
scene: 前台接到一通电话，对方仔细询问了房价和早餐时间。 The enquiry was passed to the manager for a full answer.
sceneCN: 这里 enquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获取信息而提出的问题）；句意：这个询问被转给经理，以便给出完整答复。

derivatives.zh: 询问；调查
询问者
探询的

senses.title: A request for information
senses.definition: a question asked in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获取信息而提出的问题
senses.example: We received an enquiry about the price of the flat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们收到一个询问公寓价格的电话。
senses.why: The noun names the question produced by the verb enquire.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指 enquire 这个动词所产生的「问题」。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: a formal process of finding out the facts about something
senses.definitionCN: 查明某事物事实的正式程序
senses.example: A public enquiry was opened into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 针对这起事故启动了公开调查。
senses.why: A sustained set of questions becomes an official inquiry with its own procedure.
senses.whyCN: 持续的一连串问题会变成具有自身程序的正式调查。

senses.title: The act of asking
senses.definition: the act of asking for information rather than the question itself
senses.definitionCN: 获取信息的提问行为，而不是问题本身
senses.example: The enquiry took several days of careful checking.
senses.exampleCN: 这次询问花了好几天仔细核查。
senses.why: Like many nouns in -y, it can name the whole activity and not only its single product.
senses.whyCN: 和许多 -y 结尾的名词一样，它可指整个活动，而不只是单个产物。

intro.en: Enquiry is enquire plus the noun ending -y, from Latin inquirere, to seek into.
intro.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 加名词词尾 -y，源自拉丁语 inquirere（深入查问）。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Inquirere means to search into a matter.
items.cn: inquirere 意为深入查问一件事。

items.en: Old French enquerre supplies the en- form of the verb.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 提供动词的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English enqueren gives the noun enquere or enquiry.
items.cn: 中古英语 enqueren 产生名词 enquere 或 enquiry。

items.en: Enquiry is used for both polite questions and formal investigations.
items.cn: enquiry 既用于礼貌询问，也用于正式调查。

items.en: British English often keeps enquiry, while American English prefers inquiry.
items.cn: 英式英语常保留 enquiry，美式英语更常用 inquiry。

note.en: Enquiry is the noun of enquire, and it sits beside inquiry, question, and investigation.
note.cn: enquiry 是 enquire 的名词，与 inquiry、question、investigation 相邻。

definition_zh: 通货膨胀；充气；膨胀；夸大
definition_en: a sustained rise in the general level of prices, or the act of filling something with air and swelling it
core_image: 市场里的价签一个月换了两回，同样一袋钱能买到的面包越来越少
scene: 战后的集市上，面包的价签一个月换了两回，主妇把钱袋攥得更紧，摊主还在往上改数字。 Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
sceneCN: 这里 inflation 指「一般物价水平持续上涨」（第 1 个义项：整体物价持续上升、货币购买力随之下降）；句意为物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价签、面包篮、钱袋、记账板。

senses.title: A sustained rise in the price level
senses.definition: a continuing increase in the general level of prices, so that money buys less over time
senses.definitionCN: 整体物价水平持续上升，使同样多的钱随时间买到的东西越来越少
senses.example: Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
senses.exampleCN: 物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。
senses.why: The image is a balloon being blown up: the stock of money or the level of prices swells, and the metaphor became the standard economic term in the nineteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 意象是被吹胀的气球：货币量或物价水平鼓起来，这个比喻在 19 世纪成了标准经济术语。

senses.title: The act of filling with air
senses.definition: the act of filling a tyre, balloon or other container with air or gas
senses.definitionCN: 往轮胎、气球或其他容器中注入空气或气体的动作
senses.example: Inflation of the raft took twenty minutes with a hand pump.
senses.exampleCN: 用手动气泵给救生筏充气花了二十分钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the Latin verb meant to blow into something, and the noun simply names that action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：拉丁动词意为「吹入某物」，名词只是给这个动作命名。

senses.title: The state of being swollen
senses.definition: the condition of something that has been blown up and now bulges or expands
senses.definitionCN: 某物被充气后鼓起或胀大的状态
senses.example: The doctor noted a slight inflation below the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到膝盖下方有轻微肿胀。
senses.why: From the action the noun moves to its result, so inflation can name a bulge in a body or a material.
senses.whyCN: 名词从动作转向结果，因此 inflation 也能指身体或材料上的鼓包。

senses.title: Exaggeration in speech
senses.definition: a swelling of language in which praise, claims or promises are blown up beyond the facts
senses.definitionCN: 语言上的膨胀，即赞美、主张或承诺被吹到超出事实的程度
senses.example: The brochure's claims were pure inflation of a modest trial.
senses.exampleCN: 宣传册里的说法，只是把一次小规模试验大大吹胀。
senses.why: The same balloon image serves rhetoric: words are pumped up until they no longer match the thing described.
senses.whyCN: 同一个气球意象也服务于修辞：词被吹大，直到与所描述之物不再相称。

senses.title: The inflation rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the pace at which the general level of prices is rising
senses.definitionCN: 表示整体物价水平上涨速度的百分数
senses.example: The inflation rate fell to three percent after the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 秋收之后，通胀率降到百分之三。
senses.why: A process noun readily stands for its own measure, which is why the word can be placed directly before rate.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词很容易转指自身的度量，因此这个词可以直接放在 rate 之前。

senses.title: Demand-pull inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by spending that outruns the supply of goods available
senses.definitionCN: 由支出超过现有商品供给所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Demand-pull inflation showed up first in building materials.
senses.exampleCN: 需求拉动型通胀最先出现在建筑材料上。
senses.why: When buyers bid more than the stock can answer, the rise is traced to the demand side and named accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 当买方的出价超过存货所能应付的量，上涨就被追溯到需求一侧，并据此命名。

senses.title: Cost-push inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by higher wages, energy or material costs being passed on to buyers
senses.definitionCN: 由工资、能源或材料成本上升并转嫁给买方所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Cost-push inflation followed the doubling of fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格翻倍之后，出现了成本推动型通胀。
senses.why: The same rise can be traced from the producer's costs rather than from the buyer's demand, giving the mirror term.
senses.whyCN: 同样的上涨也可以从生产者的成本而非买方的需求去追溯，于是有了这个镜像说法。

senses.title: Runaway hyperinflation
senses.definition: inflation that accelerates beyond control until the currency ceases to serve as a store of value
senses.definitionCN: 加速到无法控制、直至货币不再能保值的地步的通胀
senses.example: Hyperinflation ended with banknotes carried in wheelbarrows.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通胀以用独轮车推钞票收场。
senses.why: At the extreme the balloon bursts, and a separate word takes over to mark that the ordinary measure has failed.
senses.whyCN: 到了极端，气球炸开，另有一个词接手，标记常规度量已经失效。

intro.en: Inflation comes from Latin inflatio 'a blowing into, a swelling', built on inflare 'to blow into', from in- 'in' and flare 'to blow'. The economic sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inflation 来自拉丁 inflatio「吹入、膨胀」，由 inflare「吹入」构成，即 in-「进入」加 flare「吹」。经济义是 19 世纪才有的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Flare meant 'to blow, to breathe out'; it is the source of several English words about blowing and breathing.
items.cn: flare 意为「吹、呼出气」；英语中若干与吹气、呼吸有关的词都源于它。

items.en: In- 'into' plus flare produced inflare 'to blow into, to puff up', used of breath, wind and swollen things.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 flare 构成 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」，用于气息、风与鼓胀之物。

items.en: The noun inflatio named both the act of blowing into something and the swelling that followed.
items.cn: 名词 inflatio 既指吹入某物的动作，也指随之而来的肿胀。

items.en: English inflation is recorded from the seventeenth century in medical and natural-philosophical writing for swelling and the filling of a space with air.
items.cn: 英语 inflation 自 17 世纪见于医学与自然哲学写作，指肿胀以及用空气充满某处。

items.en: The monetary use is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when an excessive issue of money was pictured as blowing the currency up like a balloon.
items.cn: 货币义一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，当时把过量发行货币想象成把通货像气球一样吹胀。

items.en: Source uncertain (first monetary citation): the metaphor is plain, but the earliest printed use in the price sense is disputed and may belong to a later decade, so no firm date is given here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（货币义的最早书证）：比喻本身清楚，但物价义最早的印刷用例有争议，可能晚数十年，此处不给出确定年代。

note.en: The first group holds the opposite process, the verb behind this noun, and one word that only looks similar; the second holds phrases for rising prices of different breadth.
note.cn: 第一组是相反的过程、本名词背后的动词，以及一个只是长得像的词；第二组是范围不同的「物价上涨」说法。

entries.definition: The mirror image: prices fall and the currency gains purchasing power instead of losing it.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像过程：物价下跌，货币购买力上升而非下降。

entries.definition: To fill with air or to push prices up; the noun inflation names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 充气，或把价格推高；名词 inflation 指这个过程或其结果。

entries.definition: Describes forces or pressure that produce inflation; it does not name the rise itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述造成通胀的力量或压力；它不指上涨本身。

entries.definition: From Latin flectere 'to bend', not flare 'to blow': it means a bend in pitch or a change in word form, and is no relative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 flectere「弯曲」，而非 flare「吹」：指语调的弯折或词形变化，并非同族。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for higher prices; it can describe one item, while inflation implies the general level.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指价格上涨；可指单件商品，而 inflation 暗示整体水平。

entries.definition: Names the rise as households feel it through the basket of goods they buy.
entries.definitionCN: 从家庭角度命名上涨，即通过日常购买的一篮子商品感受到的涨价。

entries.definition: A general word for something intensifying; it carries no economic measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某事物加剧升级；不带经济度量含义。

entries.definition: Growth in size, volume or output; it can accompany inflation but does not mean it.
entries.definitionCN: 指尺寸、体积或产出的扩大；可与通胀同时发生，但并不等于通胀。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' plus flare 'to blow': to blow into something until it swells.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 flare「吹」：往某物里吹，直到它鼓起来。

normal.en: The family runs inflate, inflation, inflationary, inflator, deflate, deflation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：inflate、inflation、inflationary、inflator、deflate、deflation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: inflation rate, double-digit inflation, curb inflation, inflation target.
normal.cn: 固定说法：通胀率、两位数通胀、抑制通胀、通胀目标。

normal.en: The balloon image survives: an over-issued currency is a balloon blown too full.
normal.cn: 气球意象仍在：超发的货币就是吹得太满的气球。

normal.en: Do not confuse the root with flectere 'to bend', which gives inflection.
normal.cn: 别把词根与 flectere「弯曲」混淆，后者给出 inflection。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag rewritten while the ink is still wet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，墨迹未干就被改写。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon that keeps filling until the skin is thin and shiny.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球不断充气，表皮变得又薄又亮。

abstract.en: Picture a purse that stays the same size while the bread inside it shrinks.
abstract.cn: 想象钱袋大小不变，里面的面包却越变越小。

examples.en: Central banks raise rates when inflation refuses to fall.
examples.cn: 当通胀迟迟不降时，央行会加息。

examples.en: Household surveys show that inflation is felt most sharply in food prices.
examples.cn: 家庭调查显示，通胀在食品价格上感受最尖锐。

examples.en: The report blamed wage inflation for the rise in service costs.
examples.cn: 报告把服务成本上升归因于工资推动的物价上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（向内）+ flat（气）+ ion」——往里面打气，越打越鼓 → 膨胀、通胀

root: 拉丁 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」= in-「进入」+ flare「吹」→ 名词 inflatio「吹入、肿胀」→ 英语 inflation；经济义为 19 世纪比喻用法，最早书证存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: air is blown into something, it swells, and the same swelling is then applied to prices, to a measured rate, to demand, to costs and finally to a runaway spiral.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把气吹入某物，它鼓起来；同一个「鼓起」再依次用于物价、一个测得的比率、需求、成本，最后是失控的螺旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon blown fuller and fuller while the same purse buys less bread.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球越吹越满，同一个钱袋买到的面包却越来越少。

branches.en: PRICE AND RATE: the swollen level of prices is then expressed as a percentage.
branches.cn: 物价与比率：鼓起的物价水平随后被表示为一个百分数。

branches.en: AIR AND BODY: the physical act of blowing fills a thing, and the thing bulges.
branches.cn: 气与物体：吹入的物理动作把东西充满，东西便鼓起。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: the same swelling shows up in speech as exaggeration and self-praise.
branches.cn: 语言：同一种「鼓起」在言语中表现为夸大与自夸。

branches.en: DEMAND AND COST: prices can be pushed from the buyer's side or pulled from the producer's side.
branches.cn: 需求与成本：物价可由买方一侧推起，也可由生产者一侧拉起。

branches.en: RUNAWAY: at the extreme the balloon bursts into hyperinflation.
branches.cn: 失控：到了极端，气球炸成恶性通胀。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a Latin noun suffix; each piece also builds other English words, and the family has a mirror image in de-.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个拉丁名词后缀构成；每一段还构成别的英语词，整个词族还有一个以 de- 开头的镜像形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare 'to blow' gives inflate, inflation, deflate, deflation and flatus; in- and de- set the two directions of the same image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flare「吹」衍生出 inflate、inflation、deflate、deflation 与 flatus；in- 与 de- 标出同一意象的两个方向。

items.example: The prefix points the blowing inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「吹」指向内部。

items.example: The root carries the idea of moving air.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「推动空气」的意思。

items.meaning: to blow into; to puff up
items.example: The compound names both the act and its swelling result.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式既指动作，也指其鼓胀的结果。

items.example: The Latin noun supplied the English word directly.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词直接提供了英语词。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: to fill with air; to raise prices
items.example: Dealers inflate prices before a sale.
items.exampleCN: 商家会在促销前抬高价格。

items.meaning: to let air out; to lower prices
items.example: The mirror verb was formed by swapping the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个镜像动词是靠替换前缀造出的。

items.example: The adjective describes pressure, not the rise itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述压力，而非上涨本身。

definition_en: in a clear and exact way, or for one particular purpose or thing only
core_image: 手指点在名单上的一个名字：只此一个，别无其他
scene: 会议纪要很长，主持人用笔尖停在其中一行。 The funds were released specifically for classroom repairs.
sceneCN: 这里 specifically 是「特意地、专门地」（第 1 个义项：明确限定于某一目的）；句意为这笔资金是专门为教室维修而拨付的。图中可辨识物件：会议纪要、笔、长桌。

pos.zh: 副词：明确地；特意地；专门地

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础，义为「明确的；特定的」
由形容词 specific 加名词后缀构成，义为「明确性；特异性」

senses.title: For one particular purpose
senses.definition: for one particular purpose or use and no other
senses.definitionCN: 专为某一特定目的或用途，不含其他
senses.example: The grant was given specifically for clean-water projects.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款是专门用于清洁饮水项目的。
senses.why: The finger lands on one name in a long list: the aim excludes everything else.
senses.whyCN: 手指落在长名单上的一个名字：这一指向排除其他一切。

senses.title: In a clear and exact way
senses.definition: in a manner that is clear, exact, and free of vagueness
senses.definitionCN: 以清楚、确切、不含糊的方式
senses.example: She specifically mentioned the broken window in her report.
senses.exampleCN: 她在报告中明确提到了那扇破窗。
senses.why: Precision is an adverb too: not only what is said, but how tightly it is said.
senses.whyCN: 精确也可以是副词：不仅在于说什么，还在于说得多紧。

senses.title: As an intensifier singling out
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something applies to one case especially
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某事尤其适用于某一情形
senses.example: The book was written specifically for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是专为初学者写的。
senses.why: The pointing finger presses harder: not just one case, but only that case.
senses.whyCN: 指点的手指更用力：不只是一个情形，而是只有那个情形。

senses.title: To narrow a statement further
senses.definition: used when making a previous statement more exact, often as more specifically
senses.definitionCN: 用于把先前的表述说得更确切，常用 more specifically
senses.example: The road passes farmland; more specifically, abandoned orchards.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过农田；更确切地说，是废弃的果园。
senses.why: Each narrowing is one more click of the lens toward the single point.
senses.whyCN: 每收窄一次，镜头就向唯一点再拧近一格。

senses.title: In stated detail, item by item
senses.definition: with each item stated in detail rather than left general
senses.definitionCN: 逐项详述而非笼统带过
senses.example: The safety rules were specifically listed in the manual.
senses.exampleCN: 安全规则在手册中被逐项明确列出。
senses.why: The lens moves down the list, lighting one line after another.
senses.whyCN: 放大镜沿清单下移，逐行照亮。

senses.title: By name and not by description
senses.definition: by naming the very thing, instead of describing a class of things
senses.definitionCN: 指名确切对象，而非描述一类东西
senses.example: The rule named the bridge specifically, not bridges in general.
senses.exampleCN: 规则具体指名了那座桥，而不是泛指桥梁。
senses.why: Naming is the sharpest form of pointing: no description, just the name.
senses.whyCN: 指名是最锋利的指点方式：没有描述，只有名字。

senses.title: In technical usage: for a defined target
senses.titleCN: 技术用法：针对既定目标
senses.definition: in technical language, directed at a clearly defined target or condition
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语言中，指向清晰界定的目标或条件
senses.example: The antenna is tuned specifically to this frequency band.
senses.exampleCN: 这根天线专门调谐到这个频段。
senses.why: Engineering borrows the pointing image: the beam goes to one defined target.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用指向意象：波束只射向一个既定目标。

senses.title: When excluding by contrast
senses.definition: used to contrast the named case with everything not named
senses.definitionCN: 用于把被指名的情形与其他未指名者对比
senses.example: The discount applies to students specifically, not to staff.
senses.exampleCN: 折扣只面向学生，不面向教职工。
senses.why: The single lit point defines a dark background: what is excluded sharpens what is chosen.
senses.whyCN: 唯一被照亮之点界定了黑暗背景：被排除者使被选择者更清晰。

intro.en: Specifically is the adverb of specific, and it inherits the whole Latin story of looking and naming a kind.
intro.cn: specifically 是 specific 的副词形式，完整继承了拉丁语「观看并指名一个种类」的故事。

items.en: *spek- is generally reconstructed as "to observe"; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *spek- 表示「观察」；更早来源不确定。

items.en: Species meant "a kind, appearance", from specere "to look".
items.cn: 拉丁语 species 意为「种类、外貌」，由 specere「看」派生。

items.en: Specificus meant "constituting a kind of its own".
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 specificus 意为「自成一种的」。

items.en: The adjective specific entered English in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 形容词 specific 于十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: The adverb formed with -ly spread into everyday, legal and technical prose.
items.cn: 加 -ly 构成的副词扩展到日常、法律与技术文体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of precision and purpose.
note.cn: 形近组收同族词与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示精确与目的的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective base meaning clear and exact; the adverb is built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词基础词，义为「明确的」，本副词由它构成。

entries.definition: A written statement of exact details; same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规格、说明书」，同一拉丁词族。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to state exactly; same family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「明确说明」，同族词。

entries.definition: Meaning in an important way; merely looks somewhat similar and is of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「显著地」；只是外形略近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A sample for study; from the same seeing root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标本、样本」，出自同一「观看」词根。

entries.definition: Especially or above all; close in the singling-out sense.
entries.definitionCN: 尤其、首要地，与「单独挑出」义接近。

entries.definition: Exactly and correctly; overlaps the clarity sense.
entries.definitionCN: 精确正确地，与「明确」义项重叠。

entries.definition: In a plainly stated, open way.
entries.definitionCN: 明白直陈地。

entries.definition: Formally and clearly stated, often legal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 正式明确地，常用于法律语气。

entries.definition: Used to introduce the exact item meant.
entries.definitionCN: 用于引出确切所指的一项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word family and the common phrases where the adverb appears.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用词族知识和该副词常出现的搭配。

normal.en: The adverb simply adds -ly to specific: precision in motion.
normal.cn: 本副词由 specific 加 -ly 构成：精确的动态形式。

normal.en: Specifically for means set aside for that purpose only.
normal.cn: specifically for 表示专门留给那个用途。

normal.en: More specifically narrows a statement one step further.
normal.cn: more specifically 把表述再收窄一步。

normal.en: The same family gives specify and specification.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 specify 与 specification。

normal.en: The adverb often excludes: for students specifically, not staff.
normal.cn: 这个副词常带排除意味：只面向学生，不面向教职工。

abstract.en: Picture a finger on a guest list: it rests on one name and slides past all the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指停在宾客名单上：只按住一个名字，滑过其余。

abstract.en: The adverb is a spotlight with a very narrow beam.
abstract.cn: 这个副词是一束极窄的聚光灯。

abstract.en: Each use of more specifically turns one knob of the lens tighter.
abstract.cn: 每用一次 more specifically，镜头就再拧紧一格。

examples.en: The van was bought specifically for delivering meals.
examples.cn: 这辆货车是专门为送餐而购置的。

examples.en: He specifically asked that no one touch the archive boxes.
examples.cn: 他明确要求谁都不许碰档案箱。

examples.en: The survey focused on commuters, specifically bicycle riders.
examples.cn: 调查聚焦通勤者，尤其是骑自行车的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯比西菲克利」——手指点名单只按一个：专门地；明确地

root: specifically 由形容词 specific 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；specific 来自晚期拉丁语 specificus「自成一种的」，其词根 species「种类」源自 specere「观看」；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb senses all point: for one purpose only, stated exactly, or narrowing a claim step by step.
sensesIntro.cn: 本副词各义项都在「指向」：只为一目的、表述确切，或逐步收窄表述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger resting on one name in a long list, all others sliding past.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指按住长名单上的一个名字，其余滑过。

branches.en: THE AIM LINE: the beam is set for one purpose and stated without haze.
branches.cn: 目的线：光束为一目的而设，表述无雾。

branches.en: THE EMPHASIS LINE: not just one case, but only that case, even in technical tuning.
branches.cn: 强调线：不止一个情形，而是只有那个情形，技术调谐亦然。

branches.en: THE NARROWING LINE: each step of more specifically clicks the lens tighter.
branches.cn: 收窄线：more specifically 每一步都把镜头拧紧一格。

branches.en: THE NAMING LINE: items listed one by one, and finally by bare name.
branches.cn: 指名线：逐项列出，最终直呼其名。

branches.en: THE EXCLUSION LINE: the dark background around the lit point defines the choice.
branches.cn: 排除线：照亮之点四周的黑暗背景界定出选择。

intro.en: The word stacks a Latin kind-root, a Late Latin making suffix, and the English adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词叠合了拉丁「种类」词根、晚期拉丁「做成」后缀与英语副词结尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are recorded; only the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式均有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The root is shared by the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 该词根为整个词族共享。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb.
The same seeing root forms speculate.
items.exampleCN: 同一「观看」词根构成 speculate。

latinEntries.meaning: constituting a kind of its own

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词基础，义为「明确的；特定的」
