definition_zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；在…范围内变动；靶场
definition_en: a set of different things of the same type; the limits within which something varies; the distance a weapon or signal can reach; a line of connected mountains; to vary between two limits; a place for shooting practice
core_image: 一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度从这头排到那头
scene: 清晨的靶场里，射手把标尺架好，远处的山脊像一条长线铺到天边。 The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
sceneCN: 这里 range 是「射程」（第 3 个义项：武器能打到的距离）；句意为这支步枪的射程接近一千米。画面里可留意：架起的标尺、远处的山脊、靶场尽头的靶子。

pos.zh: 范围；幅度；射程；山脉；靶场

derivatives.zh: range 加前缀 a-，指按次序摆放、安排
arrange 加 -ment，指排列方式或安排
range 加 -er，指在荒野巡逻的人
range 加 -y，指身形修长、四肢舒展的

senses.title: A set of varieties
senses.definition: a set of different things of the same type, or the limits within which something varies
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物的一个系列，或某物变动的限度
senses.example: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。
senses.why: From a row of things laid out in order came the idea of a whole series of varieties under one name.
senses.whyCN: 从「按次序排开的一行」生出「同类事物构成的一整个系列」这一概念。

senses.title: A line of mountains
senses.definition: a series of connected hills or mountains forming a long line
senses.definitionCN: 连成一条长线的一串丘陵或山峰
senses.example: A mountain range runs along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一条山脉沿着边境延伸。
senses.why: Mountains seen from a distance stand in a long row, so the row word was applied to them directly.
senses.whyCN: 远望群山时它们排成长长一行，于是这个「行」的词被直接用在山上。

senses.title: The distance a weapon reaches
senses.definition: the distance over which a gun, missile or signal can reach its target
senses.definitionCN: 枪、导弹或信号能够到达目标的距离
senses.example: The rifle had a range of nearly a thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这支步枪的射程接近一千米。
senses.why: Gunners measured how far a shot could travel, and that measured extent was called its range.
senses.whyCN: 炮手会测量一发炮弹能飞多远，这段被测出的距离就称作它的 range。

senses.title: To vary between limits
senses.definition: to vary between two fixed limits, used of prices, sizes, temperatures and the like
senses.definitionCN: 在两个固定限度之间变动，用于价格、尺寸、温度等
senses.example: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。
senses.why: Once range named the limits themselves, the verb could describe anything moving between them.
senses.whyCN: range 一旦指限度本身，动词便可用来说明任何在限度之间移动的事物。

senses.title: A place for shooting practice
senses.definition: an area laid out with targets where people practise shooting
senses.definitionCN: 排布着靶子、供人练习射击的场地
senses.example: The recruits spent the morning at the shooting range.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们在射击场度过了一个上午。
senses.why: A range is also a measured stretch of ground, and a shooting ground is exactly that: a marked extent with targets.
senses.whyCN: range 也指一段测好的地面，而射击场正是如此：一片标好的、设有靶子的场地。

intro.en: Range comes from Old French range, a row or line, probably from a Frankish word for a ring of men; all its senses grew from the idea of things set out in order.
intro.cn: range 来自古法语 range（一行、一列），可能源自法兰克语中表示一圈人的词；所有义项都从「按次序排开」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: Old French range meant a row or line, and it named things placed in order.
items.cn: 古法语 range 意为一行或一列，用来命名按次序摆放的东西。

items.en: The word is traced to a Frankish term for a ring or band of men, which gave the idea of a line.
items.cn: 这个词可追溯到法兰克语中表示一圈或一队人的词，由此产生「一行」的概念。

items.en: Middle English used range for a row and a rank, and then for the extent something could cover.
items.cn: 中古英语用 range 指一排、一列，随后又指某物所能覆盖的范围。

items.en: Gunners spoke of the range of a shot, and the word became the measured distance a weapon could reach.
items.cn: 炮手们会说一发炮弹的 range，这个词便成了武器能到达的实测距离。

items.en: Modern English extends range to mountains, to variation between limits, and to grounds for shooting practice.
items.cn: 现代英语把 range 扩展到山脉、限度之间的变动，以及练习射击的场地。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same row-and-line idea; the near-meaning group gathers words for extent and distance.
note.cn: 形近组收基于同一「排列成行」概念构成的词；近义组收表示范围与距离的词。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按特定次序摆放。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order.
entries.definitionCN: 事物摆放的方式。

entries.definition: A person who patrols and protects a wild area.
entries.definitionCN: 巡逻并保护荒野的人。

entries.definition: A row or a position in order, a related Germanic word.
entries.definitionCN: 一行或在次序中的位置，相关的日耳曼词。

entries.definition: The area or degree that something covers.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所覆盖的面积或程度。

entries.definition: The range of what something deals with.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所涉及的范围。

entries.definition: The distance or time from one end to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一端到另一端的距离或时间。

entries.definition: The space between two points.
entries.definitionCN: 两点之间的空间。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a row, then widens into a series, a reachable distance, a line of hills, a spread of values and a marked ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从一行开始，逐步扩展为系列、可达的距离、连绵的山、数值的跨度，以及标好的场地。

normal.en: Range and arrange share the same old row, one naming the line and the other the act of setting it out.
normal.cn: range 与 arrange 共享同一个古老的「行」，一个命名这条线，一个命名把线排开的行为。

normal.en: A mountain range is simply mountains standing in a long row.
normal.cn: 一条 mountain range 就是排成长长一行的山。

normal.en: A rifle's range is how far its shot can travel before it falls.
normal.cn: 步枪的 range 是子弹在落下之前能飞多远。

normal.en: When prices range from low to high, they vary between two limits.
normal.cn: 当价格 range from low to high，它们就在两个限度之间变动。

normal.en: A shooting range is a field laid out with targets for practice.
normal.cn: shooting range 是排好靶子供练习的场地。

abstract.en: Range names the space between a starting point and a limit, whether in distance, price or ability.
abstract.cn: range 是「起点与限度之间的空间」这个词，无论那空间在距离、价格还是能力上。

abstract.en: To say something is out of range is to say it lies beyond where your reach stops.
abstract.cn: 说某物 out of range，就是说它落在你触及范围的边界之外。

abstract.en: A wide range is not just many things but many things set side by side in order.
abstract.cn: a wide range 不只是许多东西，而是许多东西按次序并排摆开。

examples.en: The shop sells a wide range of teas.
examples.cn: 这家店出售种类繁多的茶。

examples.en: The missile has a range of over two thousand kilometres.
examples.cn: 这种导弹的射程超过两千公里。

examples.en: Temperatures range from ten to thirty degrees here.
examples.cn: 这里的气温在十到三十度之间变动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「软尺」——把软尺拉开来量，从这头到那头都是范围，记住 range 是范围、射程、山脉。

root: 古法语 range（一行、一列）→ 中古英语 range → 现代英语 range；可能与法兰克语「一圈人」有关。同族有 arrange、arrangement、ranger。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a row laid out in order; the senses move from a series of varieties to a line of mountains, the reach of a weapon, variation between limits and a shooting ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按次序排开的一行；义项从同类系列，到山脉，再到武器可达的距离、限度之间的变动，以及射击场地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft measuring tape stretched out, its marks running in a straight row.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把拉伸开的软尺，刻度排成笔直的一行。

branches.en: a shelf of bottles lined up in a row
branches.cn: 一排摆开的瓶子

branches.en: ridges running to the horizon
branches.cn: 延伸至地平线的山脊

branches.en: a marked distance on a rifle sight
branches.cn: 步枪准星上标出的距离

branches.en: a thermometer rising and falling
branches.cn: 上下浮动的温度计

branches.en: targets standing at the far end of a field
branches.cn: 立在场地尽头的靶子

intro.en: The word is a borrowing from Old French, and its family is built with English prefixes, suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词借自古法语，其词族由英语前缀、后缀与复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word; the older root is Frankish.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录；更早的词根是法兰克语。

definition_zh: 出口；输出；出口商品
definition_en: to send goods to another country; to spread ideas or skills abroad; goods sold abroad
core_image: 装满货物的集装箱驶向海外港口
scene: 这家公司向欧洲出口机器。 The company exports machines to Europe.
sceneCN: 这里 export 是「出口货物」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家公司向欧洲出口机器。

derivatives.zh: 出口商；出口国
出口；输出
出口的

senses.title: Sell goods abroad
senses.definition: to send goods to another country for sale
senses.definitionCN: 把货物运往另一国家销售
senses.example: The country exports coffee and bananas.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家出口咖啡和香蕉。
senses.why: The core sense is carrying goods out.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是把货物运出去。

senses.title: Spread ideas abroad
senses.definition: to spread ideas, skills, or culture to other places
senses.definitionCN: 把思想、技术或文化传播到其他地方
senses.example: The university exports its teaching methods.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学输出自己的教学方法。
senses.why: Goods are replaced by ideas that travel out.
senses.whyCN: 货物被向外传播的思想所取代。

senses.title: Goods sold abroad
senses.definition: goods or services sold to another country
senses.definitionCN: 卖到另一国家的商品或服务
senses.example: Oil is the country's main export.
senses.exampleCN: 石油是这个国家的主要出口商品。
senses.why: The action becomes the thing being sent.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成被运出的东西。

intro.en: Export comes from Latin exportare, to carry out, from ex- out and portare to carry.
intro.cn: export 来自拉丁语 exportare（运出去），由 ex-（向外）与 portare（搬运）构成。

items.en: Ex- means out.
items.cn: ex- 意为向外。

items.en: Portare means to carry.
items.cn: portare 意为搬运。

items.en: Exportare means to carry out.
items.cn: exportare 意为运出去。

items.en: Export names trade that sends goods away.
items.cn: export 指把货物运往外的贸易。

items.en: Export also covers ideas and services.
items.cn: 现代英语中 export 也涵盖思想与服务。

note.en: Export means send out; import means bring in.
note.cn: export 是运出去，import 则是运进来。

entries.definition: to bring goods into a country
entries.definitionCN: 进口

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 专家

entries.definition: to become larger
entries.definitionCN: 扩大

entries.definition: to send goods somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 运送

entries.definition: to carry from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 运输

entries.definition: to give something for money
entries.definitionCN: 出售

normalIntro.en: Export is about goods and ideas carried out of a country.
normalIntro.cn: export 指货物与思想被运出一个国家。

normal.en: Brazil exports coffee to many countries.
normal.cn: 巴西向许多国家出口咖啡。

normal.en: The firm exports software to Asia.
normal.cn: 这家公司向亚洲出口软件。

normal.en: Tea was once a major export of China.
normal.cn: 茶叶曾是中国的主要出口商品。

normal.en: New rules made exporting easier.
normal.cn: 新规定让出口变得更容易。

normal.en: The port handles exports every day.
normal.cn: 这个港口每天处理出口货物。

abstract.en: Picture a ship loaded with boxes leaving port.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘装满箱子的船驶离港口。

abstract.en: Imagine a teacher sharing a method with another country.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老师把方法传到另一个国家。

abstract.en: Think of a map with arrows pointing outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，箭头全都指向外面。

examples.en: They export wine to Europe and America.
examples.cn: 他们把葡萄酒出口到欧洲和美洲。

examples.en: The country depends on oil exports.
examples.cn: 这个国家依赖石油出口。

examples.en: The company began exporting last year.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年开始出口。

dict_mnemonic.text: ex（向外）加 port（搬运）：把货物搬向国外，就是 export（出口）。

root: 源自拉丁语 exportare（运出去），由 ex-（向外）与 portare（搬运）构成，核心义「把货物或观念运出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Export means to sell goods abroad, to spread ideas outward, or goods sold abroad.
sensesIntro.cn: export 意为向国外销售货物、向外传播思想，或出口商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a container ship heading for a foreign port.
core.cn: 核心意象：驶向海外港口的集装箱船。

branches.en: The base sense is sending goods abroad.
branches.cn: 基础义是把货物运往国外。

branches.en: Goods are replaced by ideas that travel out.
branches.cn: 货物被向外传播的思想取代。

branches.en: The action becomes the goods themselves.
branches.cn: 动作变成货物本身。

branches.en: Trade and cultural spread both move outward.
branches.cn: 贸易与文化传播都向外流动。

branches.en: The act of exporting and the exports themselves are linked.
branches.cn: 出口行为与出口商品相互关联。

intro.en: Export is built on Latin ex- out and portare to carry, the same root as transport.
intro.cn: export 由拉丁语 ex-（向外）与 portare（搬运）构成，与 transport 同根。

latinIntro.en: Latin exportare, portare, and the prefix ex- are the source elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exportare、portare 与前缀 ex- 是来源要素。

items.meaning: to send goods abroad or such goods
items.example: They export rice to nearby markets.
items.exampleCN: 他们把大米出口到邻近市场。

items.structure: English verb form and plural noun
items.meaningCN: 出口（第三人称）；出口商品
items.exampleCN: 这个国家的出口大幅上升。

items.example: The exported fruit arrives by sea.
items.exampleCN: 出口的水果经海运输达。
出口需要仔细处理文书。

items.meaning: a person or country that exports
items.example: China is a major exporter of electronics.
items.exampleCN: 中国是电子产品的主要出口国。

items.example: The law controls the exportation of arms.

items.meaning: to carry from place to place

items.exampleCN: -port 出现在 export 与 import 中。

definition_zh: 设计；图案；意图
definition_en: to plan how something will look or work, or the plan itself
core_image: 桌上摊着一张画满线条的纸，一支笔在纸上落下第一个点
scene: 几个人围着桌子，把草图上的椅子腿改了三遍才点头。 They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
sceneCN: 这里 design 指「设计」（第 1 个义项：为某物的外形或功能事先作计划）；句意是他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。

derivatives.zh: 设计师
有意的；精心安排的
有企图的；设计用的
重新设计

senses.title: Plan a shape before making it
senses.definition: to plan and draw the shape or working of something before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 在动手制作之前计划并画出某物的形状或运作方式
senses.example: They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。
senses.why: The hand tries a thing on paper so that mistakes cost only ink.
senses.whyCN: 手先在纸上试一遍，出错只费掉墨水。

senses.title: The look that was planned
senses.definition: the way something has been planned, shaped or decorated
senses.definitionCN: 某物被规划、造型或装饰出来的样子
senses.example: The carpet has a simple design of leaves and lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地毯有一幅由叶子和线条构成的简洁图案。
senses.why: What began as a plan settles into a visible pattern.
senses.whyCN: 起初只是计划，最后落成看得见的纹样。

senses.title: A purpose kept hidden
senses.definition: a purpose or plan, often one that is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 某一目的或计划，常指未明说出来的
senses.example: He asked the question by design, not by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 他问那个问题是故意的，并非偶然。
senses.why: A plan that stays in the head still shapes what the hands do.
senses.whyCN: 留在脑子里的计划，同样会塑造双手的动作。

intro.en: Design comes from Latin designare, to mark out, built on de- and signum, a sign, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: design 来自拉丁语 designare，意为标出，由 de- 与 signum（记号）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Signum was a mark or a sign, and designare meant to mark something out.
items.cn: signum 是记号或标志，designare 指把某物标出来。

items.en: It could also mean to appoint a person or sketch a plan.
items.cn: 它也可以指指定某人，或勾画一份计划。

items.en: Dessigner carried the sense of drawing and intending.
items.cn: dessigner 同时带着画图与打算的意思。

items.en: English used it for a drawing, a plan and a hidden purpose.
items.cn: 英语用它表示图样、计划与隐藏的目的。

items.en: Industry made the drawing sense the dominant one.
items.cn: 工业让「图样」这一层成了最主要的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sign element, and the meaning group all put a shape on paper before it exists.
note.cn: 形近组共用 sign 这一层，近义组则都表示在实物出现前先把形状放到纸上。

entries.definition: to name someone for a duty
entries.definitionCN: 指定某人担任某职

entries.definition: a person who plans how things look
entries.definitionCN: 规划事物外观的人

entries.definition: secretly planning to get something
entries.definitionCN: 暗中图谋的

entries.definition: to decide in advance how to do something
entries.definitionCN: 事先决定如何做某事

entries.definition: to write or draw a first rough version
entries.definitionCN: 写出或画出第一份粗略稿

entries.definition: a repeated shape used for decoration
entries.definitionCN: 用于装饰的重复图形

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a pencil dot on blank paper and end with a pattern that repeats on cloth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从白纸上一个铅笔点开始，落到布上反复出现的花纹。

normal.en: A design is a mistake you are allowed to make on paper.
normal.cn: 设计就是允许你先在纸上犯的那个错。

normal.en: De- plus signum is marking a place so the hand can find it.
normal.cn: de- 加 signum，就是标出一个位置，让手能找到。

normal.en: A chair is designed twice: once in lines, once in wood.
normal.cn: 一把椅子被设计两次：一次用线条，一次用木头。

normal.en: A pattern on a carpet is a plan that decided to stay.
normal.cn: 地毯上的图案，是决定留下来的计划。

normal.en: By design means the accident was never an accident.
normal.cn: by design 就是说那场意外从来不是意外。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil resting on an empty sheet, not yet moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一支铅笔停在空白纸面上，还没有动。

abstract.en: Picture a chair made of thin lines standing in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一把由细线组成、立在空中的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture the same leaf printed across a long roll of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象同一片叶子印在一长卷布上。

examples.en: They spent a month designing a chair that would fit a small flat.
examples.cn: 他们花了一个月设计一把适合小公寓的椅子。

examples.en: The carpet has a simple design of leaves and lines.
examples.cn: 这块地毯有一幅由叶子和线条构成的简洁图案。

examples.en: He asked the question by design, not by accident.
examples.cn: 他问那个问题是故意的，并非偶然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 design 记成「地赛恩」：de 向下，sign 是记号，把想法一笔笔记成记号，就是设计。

root: 来自拉丁语 designare，由 de-（向下）与 signum（记号）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是标出、画下记号，后来指在制作前规划形状，也指规划出来的图案，还保留着心里的意图这一层。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan tried on paper, to the pattern it leaves, to a purpose kept inside the head.
sensesIntro.cn: 从在纸上试演的计划，到它留下的图案，再到藏在脑子里的意图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn on paper before anything is built.
core.cn: 核心意象：动手之前先落在纸上的一条线。

branches.en: The first sense is the act of drawing the plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把计划画出来的那个动作。

branches.en: The second sense is what the plan looks like once it settles.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是计划落定后呈现出来的样子。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan that never becomes visible.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是始终不露面的那份计划。

branches.en: Drawing a shape and the shape drawn are one word apart.
branches.cn: 画形状与画成的形状，只隔着一个词。

branches.en: A plan on paper and a plan in the mind both guide the hand.
branches.cn: 纸上的计划与心里的计划，都在引导那双手。

intro.en: Design gathers words about marking out, planning and the people who do it.
intro.cn: design 聚起一族词，关于标出、规划以及从事它的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin signum, a sign, and de- adds the act of marking something out.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 signum（记号），前缀 de- 添上把某物标出来的动作。

items.meaning: to plan a shape or purpose
one who plans how things look
items.example: The designer showed us a sketch.
items.exampleCN: 设计师给我们看了一张草图。
两位设计师分担了这项工作。

items.example: It is a well designed tool.
items.exampleCN: 这是一件设计良好的工具。

items.meaning: to plan again in a new way
items.exampleCN: 他们重新设计了整个版面。

items.meaning: to mark out for a duty
items.exampleCN: 他们指定了一间安静的屋子。

items.example: The old designation is still used.

definition_zh: 令人印象深刻的；令人赞叹的；可观的
definition_en: so good, large, or skilful that people notice it and admire it
core_image: 一座横跨河面的大桥，桥索整齐排开，让人站在桥上忘了说话
scene: 第一次走上这座横跨河面的大桥，钢索整整齐齐排开，风里有回声。 An impressive bridge, and the traffic was surprisingly quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 impressive 是「令人印象深刻的、令人赞叹的」（第 1 个义项：好到让人忍不住赞叹），句意是这是一座令人赞叹的桥，而且车流竟出奇地安静。画面里有横跨河面的大桥、整齐排开的钢索和风声。

pos.zh: 形容词：令人印象深刻的、令人赞叹的；（数量）可观的

derivatives.zh: 印象、感受；印痕
令人赞叹地
平平无奇的、不令人赞叹的

senses.title: Deserving admiration
senses.definition: so good or skilful that people admire it
senses.definitionCN: 好到或熟练到让人由衷赞叹
senses.example: Her command of three languages is impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 她掌握三种语言，令人佩服。
senses.why: The suffix -ive means having the power to do something, so impressive means able to impress.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 表示「具有……的力量」，所以 impressive 意为「能打动人的」。

senses.title: Large in scale
senses.definition: large enough in size or number to attract notice
senses.definitionCN: 在体量或数量上大到足以引人注目
senses.example: The library holds an impressive number of local maps.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆收藏的本地地图数量相当可观。
senses.why: Scale alone can create admiration, so the adjective also describes mere bigness.
senses.whyCN: 光是规模就能引发赞叹，所以这个形容词也能形容单纯的「大」。

senses.title: Making a strong effect
senses.definition: producing a strong visual or emotional effect, whether or not it is good in other ways
senses.definitionCN: 在视觉或情绪上造成强烈效果，别方面未必优秀
senses.example: The storm was impressive in its sheer noise.
senses.exampleCN: 那场暴风雨单凭声势就够惊人了。
senses.why: The word judges the strength of the effect, not always the quality behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判的是效果有多强，而不是背后的品质一定多好。

intro.en: Impressive is built with the -ive suffix on impress, so it literally means having the power to press a mark into someone.
intro.cn: impressive 是在 impress 上加 -ive 后缀构成的，字面意思是「有力量在人心里压出印子的」。

items.en: Premere meant to press, and imprimere meant to press into, leaving a mark.
items.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为「压」，imprimere 意为「压进去」，留下印痕。

items.en: The suffix -ivus marked adjectives that describe a capacity or a tendency.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 用来标记表示能力或倾向的形容词。

items.en: French formed impressif along the same lines, keeping the sense of producing an effect.
items.cn: 法语按同样思路造出 impressif，保留「产生效果」的意思。

items.en: English took impressive in the sixteenth century, at first for things that leave a strong mark on the mind.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 impressive，最初指能在人心里留下强烈印痕的事物。

items.en: Praise broadened its use, so that impressive now covers size, skill, and sheer spectacle.
items.cn: 赞美的用法把它推得更广，如今可形容规模、技艺，也可形容纯粹的场面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words close in form; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of praise.
note.cn: 形近组收外形相近的词；近义组收表示赞许的形容词。

entries.definition: Feeling admiration, said of the person rather than the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 「被打动的」，说的是人而不是物，容易与 impressive 混用。

entries.definition: The feeling or mark that is left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，指留下的感觉或印痕。

entries.definition: Able to show feeling clearly, from the opposite prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 「富有表现力的」，前缀相反，方向朝外。

entries.definition: Unusual enough to catch the eye at once.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「醒目的、引人注目的」，强调一眼就被抓住。

entries.definition: Worth talking about because it is unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「非凡的」，因不寻常而值得议论。

entries.definition: Extremely beautiful, grand, or splendid.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词「壮丽的、宏伟的」，侧重华美与气派。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the difference between the thing that impresses and the person who is impressed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住「打动人的东西」与「被打动的人」之间的区别。

normal.en: impressive ends in -ive, which marks the power to act: the thing itself does the impressing.
normal.cn: impressive 以 -ive 收尾，标记的是「有力量去作用」，是事物本身在打动人。

normal.en: You are impressed; the bridge is impressive. Change the ending to change who feels what.
normal.cn: 你是 impressed，桥是 impressive，换个词尾就换了谁在感受。

normal.en: In praise, impressive is the safe middle ground: stronger than good, weaker than extraordinary.
normal.cn: 在赞美里，impressive 是稳妥的中段：比 good 强，比 extraordinary 弱。

normal.en: Numbers can be impressive too, as in an impressive collection of stamps.
normal.cn: 数量也能令人赞叹，比如一份相当可观的邮票收藏。

normal.en: Unimpressive is the quiet way to say a thing failed to move you at all.
normal.cn: unimpressive 是委婉地说某样东西完全没打动你。

abstract.en: What counts as impressive shifts with the crowd, so praise always carries a reference group inside it.
abstract.cn: 什么叫令人赞叹随人群而变，所以每次赞许里都藏着一个参照群体。

abstract.en: The suffix says the object has force of its own, which is why we rarely call a borrowed achievement impressive.
abstract.cn: 后缀说这事物本身带着力量，所以我们很少说借来的成就令人赞叹。

abstract.en: Impressive is the vocabulary of selection: it ranks what deserves to be remembered.
abstract.cn: impressive 是筛选用的词，它给「值得被记住」排了队。

examples.en: The team made impressive progress in only six weeks.
examples.cn: 这支队伍仅用六周就取得了令人瞩目的进展。

examples.en: We were impressed by how calmly she answered.
examples.cn: 她回答得如此镇定，让我们很佩服。

examples.en: The storm was impressive, though it did little damage.
examples.cn: 那场暴风雨声势惊人，不过没造成什么破坏。

dict_mnemonic.text: impress 使留有印象 + -ive 形容词词尾——能给人压出深印的，就是令人印象深刻的

root: 在拉丁语 imprimere「压进去」的英语动词 impress 之上加形容词后缀 -ive（表示「具有……力量」），经法语 impressif 于十六世纪进入英语，词义由「能在心上留印」扩展到规模与场面。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: deserving admiration, large in scale, and strong in effect on the eye or the ear.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：值得赞叹，规模可观，以及在视听上造成强烈效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bridge whose cables are so orderly that people stop talking when they step on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座钢索排列齐整的大桥，人一踏上去就忘了说话。

branches.en: THE SKILL: impressive marks something done unusually well.
branches.cn: 技艺线：impressive 标出做得格外好的东西。

branches.en: THE SIZE: sheer quantity can carry the same weight.
branches.cn: 规模线：光是数量也能扛起同样的分量。

branches.en: THE FORCE: a storm can impress without being good.
branches.cn: 力量线：一场暴风雨可以不带善意地令人惊叹。

branches.en: THE PAIR: impressed belongs to the person, impressive to the thing.
branches.cn: 对照线：impressed 归人，impressive 归事物。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: impressively and unimpressive turn the same stem to adverb and negation.
branches.cn: 词族线：impressively 与 unimpressive 把同一词干变成副词与否定。

intro.en: The table puts -ive adjectives beside the verbs and nouns they come from.
intro.cn: 此表把 -ive 形容词与其来源的动词、名词放在一起。

latinIntro.en: The Latin -ivus tagged a capacity, and it survives in dozens of English adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 -ivus 标记的是能力，它在英语里留下了几十个形容词。

items.meaningCN: 形容词：令人印象深刻的
items.example: The hall was impressive in its size.
items.exampleCN: 那座大厅之大令人惊叹。

items.meaning: in a way that earns admiration
items.example: She finished the race impressively fast.
items.exampleCN: 她跑完比赛的速度令人赞叹。

items.example: We were impressed by the careful work.

definition_en: happening, done, or published once every week, or a publication that appears every week
core_image: 翻到日历上每周固定圈出的那一天：同一格反复出现

senses.title: Happening once every week
senses.titleCN: 每周发生的；每周一次的
senses.definition: happening once every week or every seven days
senses.definitionCN: 每七天发生一次的，按周循环进行
senses.example: Our team has a weekly meeting every Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们团队每周一早上开一次例会。
senses.why: The base word week fixes the time unit, and -ly here forms an adjective of frequency, so the image is an event that returns with every new week.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 week 锁定了时间单位，-ly 在此构成表频率的形容词，意象是「每迎来新的一周，这件事就重现一次」。

senses.title: Calculated or paid by the week
senses.titleCN: 按周计算的；按周支付的
senses.definition: calculated, counted, or paid over a period of one week
senses.definitionCN: 以一周为单位来计算、统计或支付
senses.example: Workers here are paid a weekly wage instead of a monthly salary.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的工人拿的是周薪，而不是月薪。
senses.why: Once an event is tied to the week, money or figures measured over that span inherit the same weekly frame.
senses.whyCN: 当事情与「周」绑定后，按这一时段结算的金钱或数字自然沿用同一个「按周」的框架。

senses.title: Done or used every week as a routine
senses.titleCN: 每周例行使用的；每周进行的
senses.definition: used, done, or repeated as a weekly routine or habit
senses.definitionCN: 作为每周的例行安排被使用或重复
senses.example: She writes a weekly column for the local newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 她为当地报纸撰写每周专栏。
senses.why: Repetition at fixed weekly intervals turns the adjective toward habitual practice rather than a single event.
senses.whyCN: 固定每周重复，使这个词从「一次性事件」转向「习惯性的例行做法」。

senses.title: Lasting or continuing for a week
senses.definition: lasting, continuing, or valid for the period of one week
senses.definitionCN: 为期一周、持续或有效一整周
senses.example: They rented a weekly apartment by the seaside for the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为度假在海边按周租了一套公寓。
senses.why: The week can measure not only a moment of return but also a span of duration, so weekly stretches to cover the whole seven days.
senses.whyCN: 「周」不仅能标记重现的时刻，也能度量持续的时段，weekly 于是可覆盖整整七天的跨度。

senses.title: Every week without exception
senses.definition: used to say that something happens each week as a matter of course
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事每周照例发生，无一例外
senses.example: The couple visits their parents weekly.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇每周都去看望父母。
senses.why: As an adverb of frequency, weekly compresses the whole cycle into one word: each week, again and again.
senses.whyCN: 作为频率副词，weekly 把整个周期压缩进一个词里：每一周，一次又一次。

senses.title: A publication issued every week
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine that is published once every week
senses.definitionCN: 每周出版一期的报纸或杂志
senses.example: This weekly focuses on science and technology news.
senses.exampleCN: 这本周刊聚焦科技新闻。
senses.why: When the adjective stands alone as a noun, it names the thing itself: the publication that reappears every week.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词独立成名词时，它直接指代事物本身：每周重现一次的那份出版物。

senses.title: A weekly event or series
senses.titleCN: 每周一次的活动（口语借代）
senses.definition: informal use for something that happens weekly, such as a regular gathering
senses.definitionCN: 口语中对每周固定发生之事的借代说法，如定期聚会
senses.example: Dinner at Grandma's became their weekly.
senses.exampleCN: 去奶奶家吃晚饭成了他们每周的固定活动。
senses.why: Like the magazine, a routine event can be reduced to the single word weekly, the frequency standing for the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 和周刊一样，例行活动也可以被压缩成 weekly 一个词，用频率代指活动本身。

senses.title: Weekly figures or records
senses.definition: recording or presenting data for each separate week
senses.definitionCN: 按每个独立星期记录或呈现数据
senses.example: The chart shows weekly rainfall for the whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示了整个夏天每周的降雨量。
senses.why: Data sliced into seven-day units keeps the weekly label, extending from events to measurements.
senses.whyCN: 数据被切成七天一段的单位后沿用 weekly 标签，从事件扩展到度量。

intro.en: Weekly is a transparent compound of week plus the adverbial and adjectival suffix -ly, formed inside English rather than borrowed.
intro.cn: weekly 是 week（周）加后缀 -ly 的透明组合词，在英语内部生成，并非借词。

items.en: The root *weik- is generally reconstructed with senses of turning or changing, thought to underlie words for time cycles.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *weik- 含「转动、更替」之义，被认为是一系列时间循环词的基础。

items.en: Old English wicu or wice meant a period of seven days, already the calendar unit we still use.
items.cn: 古英语 wicu／wice 意为七天的时段，已是沿用至今的历法单位。

items.en: Middle English weke carried the same meaning, and compounds with -li began to mark frequency.
items.cn: 中古英语作 weke，词义不变，与 -li 组合的派生词开始表示频率。

items.en: Weekly is attested from the fifteenth century as an adjective meaning once every week, and later as an adverb.
items.cn: weekly 自十五世纪起有记载，作形容词表示「每周一次」，后来又用作副词。

items.en: The noun use for a weekly publication became common as periodical press grew in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪报刊业兴起后，指「周刊」的名词用法逐渐普遍。

items.en: Today weekly covers the adjective, adverb, and noun senses in everyday and professional language.
items.cn: 如今 weekly 兼作形容词、副词和名词，用于日常与专业语境。

note.en: Weekly sits in a family of frequency words built on time units with -ly, and is easily confused with the adverb weekly meaning weakly.
note.cn: weekly 属于「时间单位 + -ly」的频率词家族，且与表示「虚弱地」的 weakly 发音相近，需注意区分。

entries.definition: in a weak manner; lacking strength
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱地；无力地。与 weekly 只是发音相同，词源完全不同（weak + -ly）

entries.definition: happening or appearing once every month
entries.definitionCN: 每月一次的；月刊。构词方式与 weekly 完全平行

entries.definition: happening once every year
entries.definitionCN: 每年一次的；年刊。同为时间单位加 -ly 的频率词

entries.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the end of the week
entries.definitionCN: 周末。共享词根 week，但指时段而非频率

entries.definition: an evening of a weekday
entries.definitionCN: 工作日的夜晚。同为 week 的复合词

entries.definition: happening at fixed intervals
entries.definitionCN: 定期的；规律的。泛指固定间隔，不限于一周

entries.definition: a magazine published at regular intervals
entries.definitionCN: 期刊；杂志。与周刊同类出版物，出版周期任意

entries.definition: every two weeks, or sometimes twice a week
entries.definitionCN: 两周一次的（有时指每周两次）。频率相邻，语义易混

entries.definition: happening every two weeks
entries.definitionCN: 每两周一次的（英式）。与 weekly 频率不同但同族

entries.definition: happening once every day
entries.definitionCN: 每日的；日报。更高频率的同族频率词

normalIntro.en: Weekly is easy to remember once you see week plus -ly and its frequency family.
normalIntro.cn: 看清 week 加 -ly 的结构以及整个频率词家族，weekly 就好记了。

normal.en: week + -ly: the suffix turns the time unit into a frequency word.
normal.cn: week（周）+ -ly：后缀把时间单位变成频率词。

normal.en: monthly, yearly, daily, fortnightly: one family of frequency words.
normal.cn: monthly、yearly、daily、fortnightly：同一个频率词家族。

normal.en: a weekly meeting returns every Monday.
normal.cn: weekly meeting 每周一都会回来一次。

normal.en: a weekly magazine has fifty-two issues a year.
normal.cn: 周刊一年出五十二期。

normal.en: weekly pay means your wallet is refilled every seven days.
normal.cn: weekly pay 意味着钱包每七天补一次。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the same square circled again and again, one week apart.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上同一格被反复圈出，每次相隔一周。

abstract.en: Hear a clock that chimes only on Fridays, the weekly signal.
abstract.cn: 听一座只在周五报时的钟，那就是每周一次的信号。

abstract.en: See pages of a magazine stacking up, one layer added every week.
abstract.cn: 看杂志一页页叠起来，每周加一层。

examples.en: The committee holds a weekly meeting to review progress.
examples.cn: 委员会每周开一次例会检查进展。

examples.en: Her weekly column is read by thousands of local residents.
examples.cn: 她的每周专栏被数千名当地居民阅读。

examples.en: He is paid weekly, every Friday afternoon.
examples.cn: 他按周领薪，每周五下午发放。

root: weekly 为英语本土构词：week（周，源自古英语 wicu「七天时段」，一般认为可追溯至原始印欧语词根 *weik-「转动、更替」）加副词／形容词后缀 -ly。此处 -ly 并非形容词「ly」的「像……一样」义，而是构词后缀，与 monthly、daily 同型。

sensesIntro.en: From the fixed seven-day cycle, weekly spreads from recurring events to pay, routines, duration, adverbial use, and finally the publication itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从固定的七天周期出发，weekly 由反复发生的事件扩展到薪酬、例行安排、持续时间、副词用法，最终落到出版物本身。

branches.en: recurring events harden into weekly routines
branches.cn: 反复发生的事件固化为每周例行安排

branches.en: money and data are sliced into weekly units
branches.cn: 金钱与数据被切成按周计算的单位

branches.en: the week measures duration, not just return
branches.cn: 周不仅标记重现，也度量持续时间

branches.en: as an adverb the whole cycle compresses into one word
branches.cn: 作副词时整个周期压缩进一个词

branches.en: the frequency itself names the publication and the event
branches.cn: 频率本身转而指代出版物和活动

intro.en: Weekly is built with the native suffix -ly attached to a Germanic time word, and its family shows the same pattern.
intro.cn: weekly 由本族语后缀 -ly 附加在日耳曼时间词上构成，其词族呈现相同构词模式。

latinIntro.en: As a Germanic formation, weekly has no Latin relatives; the entries below show the -ly pattern across time words.
latinIntro.cn: 作为日耳曼语构词，weekly 没有拉丁同源词；以下条目展示 -ly 在时间词上的构词模式。

definition_zh: 心情；情绪；气氛；语气（语法）；一时的兴致
definition_en: a temporary state of feeling, or the atmosphere of a place or group, or a grammatical category of the verb
core_image: 天气没有变，屋里的人却觉得整间房子忽明忽暗，像云在屋顶上走
scene: 排练到一半，指挥忽然放下手，说今天先到这里，因为整个乐队已经提不起劲。 The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
sceneCN: 这里 mood 指「一群人当下共同的情绪基调」（第 1 个义项：一时的情绪状态）；句意为指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。图中可辨识物件：放下的指挥棒、松开的谱架、空着的上半场座位；对应第 1 个义项。

情绪波动；一时的心情变化

闷闷不乐地

senses.title: A temporary state of feeling
senses.definition: the way a person feels at a particular time, seen as passing rather than fixed
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某段时间里的感受状态，被视为会过去而非固定
senses.example: The conductor stopped the rehearsal because the mood in the hall had gone flat.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥中止排练，因为大厅里的情绪已经没了劲。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply 'mind, disposition', so the word names the weather inside a person rather than their climate.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语义就是「心境、性情」，因此这个词命名的是人内部的天气，而不是气候。

senses.title: The atmosphere of a place
senses.definition: the feeling that a room, a street or a gathering gives off
senses.definitionCN: 一间屋子、一条街或一场聚会所散发出的感受
senses.example: Candles on the tables changed the mood of the whole restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上的蜡烛改变了整间餐馆的气氛。
senses.why: the same word moves from one head to a space, because a space is read as having a temper of its own.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一颗脑袋移到一个空间，因为空间被读作有自己的脾气。

senses.title: A spell of bad temper
senses.definition: a period of sulking or irritability, often named in the plural and with a possessive
senses.definitionCN: 一段闷气或易怒的时期，常以复数并带物主词出现
senses.example: He has been in one of his moods since the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 开会之后他一直闹着脾气。
senses.why: when the passing state is unpleasant, the plural turns it into a recurring event that others learn to expect.
senses.whyCN: 当这种会过去的状态并不愉快时，复数把它变成别人学会预期、一再发生的事。

senses.title: A grammatical category
senses.definition: the form of a verb that shows whether it states, commands or supposes
senses.definitionCN: 动词的形式，表明它是在陈述、命令还是假设
senses.example: English marks the imperative mood by leaving the subject out.
senses.exampleCN: 英语通过省去主语来标记祈使语气。
senses.why: this sense is a different word altogether, borrowed from Latin modus 'measure, manner', and it means a manner of speaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项其实是另一个词，借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，意思是说话的方式。

senses.title: The public's temper
senses.definition: the general temper of a group, market or electorate at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻一个群体、市场或选民的总体情绪
senses.example: The public mood turned against the plan within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一周之内公众情绪就转向反对这个方案。
senses.why: one person's weather scaled up becomes a collective climate that politicians claim to read.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的天气放大之后成为集体的气候，政治家声称自己能读出它。

senses.title: Feeling like doing something
senses.definition: the inclination to do a particular thing at a particular moment
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时刻做某件具体事情的倾向
senses.example: She was not in the mood for another long explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有兴致再听一段冗长的解释。
senses.why: the state is now aimed at an object, and 'in the mood for' turns a climate into a door that is either open or shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态现在有了对象，「有兴致」把气候变成一扇要么开、要么关的门。

senses.title: Rapid shifts of feeling
senses.definition: quick changes between emotional states, often treated as a symptom or a trait
senses.definitionCN: 情绪状态之间的快速变化，常被当作症状或特质
senses.example: Her mood swings made the household walk on glass.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起落让全家人如履薄冰。
senses.why: the plural measures frequency, turning a state into a pattern that others can chart.
senses.whyCN: 复数衡量的是频率，把一个状态变成旁人能画出来的模式。

senses.title: The key of a work
senses.definition: the prevailing feeling that a painting, film or piece of music is built to produce
senses.definitionCN: 一幅画、一部电影或一段音乐被设计来产生的总体感受
senses.example: The grey palette gives the film a mood of waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 灰调子给这部片子一种等待的基调。
senses.why: artists speak of mood because a work also has weather, and the term lets them tune it deliberately.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家谈基调，是因为作品也有天气，而这个说法让他们能刻意调它。

intro.en: English has two different words written mood. The feeling word is native Old English mod 'mind, courage, temper'. The grammar word was borrowed later from Latin modus 'measure, manner', the same source as mode and model. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个写法相同的 mood。表感受的那个是本族古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」；语法义的那个则是后来从拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」借入的，与 mode、model 同源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mod meant 'mind, inner self, courage, anger'. It is Germanic in origin and had no connection with Latin at all.
items.cn: mod 意为「心、内在自我、勇气、愤怒」。它源出日耳曼语，与拉丁语毫无关联。

items.en: As the older senses faded, the word narrowed to a passing state of feeling, the sense it carries today.
items.cn: 随着较早的义项淡出，这个词收窄为一种会过去的感受状态，也就是今天的义项。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, standard, manner'. Grammarians used it for the manner in which a verb states or commands, and that use entered English.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、标准、方式」。语法学家用它指动词陈述或命令的方式，这一用法进入了英语。

items.en: The spelling fell together in Middle English, so that one shape now carries two unrelated histories, one Germanic and one Latin.
items.cn: 两个词在中古英语里拼写合流，于是一个字形现在背着两段互不相关的历史，一段日耳曼，一段拉丁。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the feeling word was extended to rooms, crowds, markets and works of art, and mood music followed in the twentieth.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，表感受的那个词被延伸到屋子、人群、市场与艺术品，20 世纪又有了「氛围音乐」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest written forms of the Germanic word are attested but its deeper pre-Germanic origin is a reconstruction, and no first date is agreed for the grammar borrowing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个日耳曼词的最早书写形式有书证，但它在日耳曼语之前的更深来源属重构形式；语法义借入的确切年代也没有公认结论。

note.en: Group one holds the word that looks the same but has another history; group two holds feeling words that differ in duration and cause.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相同而历史不同的词；第二组是持续时间与起因不同的感受词。

entries.definition: From Latin modus 'measure, manner': a way of doing something. It looks close to mood but shares history only with the grammar sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」：做事的方式。字形近 mood，但只与语法义共享历史。

entries.definition: Built on the feeling sense: given to sudden low or irritable states.
entries.definitionCN: 由表感受的义项构成：容易陷入突然的低落或烦躁。

entries.definition: Also from modus through a small form meaning 'little measure'; it belongs to design, not to feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同样出自 modus，经由一个意为「小尺度」的形式；属设计领域，与感受无关。

entries.definition: From the same idea of measure: kept within limits. Nothing of it survives in the feeling word.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「尺度」这一观念：保持在限度之内。表感受的那个词里没有留下它的痕迹。

entries.definition: A distinct surge such as fear or joy; a mood is the longer weather that such surges happen inside.
entries.definitionCN: 如恐惧或喜悦那样一次明确的涌动；mood 是这些涌动所发生的更长的天气。

entries.definition: A settled tendency to become angry, closer to temperament than to a passing state.
entries.definitionCN: 易怒的固定倾向，更接近气质而非一时的状态。

entries.definition: The feel of a space or occasion; it covers the place sense but never the inner state of one person.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间或场合的感受；覆盖「地点」义，却从不指单个人的内在状态。

entries.definition: A plural word for how high or low someone's cheer is, as in high spirits; it measures level, not colour.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个人兴致高低的复数说法，如兴致高；衡量的是水位，而不是颜色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The feeling sense is native Old English, while the grammar sense came from Latin modus, so one spelling hides two families.
normal.cn: 感受义是本族古英语，语法义则来自拉丁 modus，因此一个拼写藏着两个词族。

normal.en: The family runs mood, moody, moodily, moodiness, mood-altering, mood board.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mood、moody、moodily、moodiness、mood-altering、mood board。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: in a good mood, in the mood for, mood swings, set the mood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：心情好、有兴致、情绪波动、定下气氛。

normal.en: Grammar keeps the Latin side alive in phrases like the imperative mood.
normal.cn: 语法在「祈使语气」一类说法里让拉丁那一面活着。

normal.en: Markets and newspapers speak of the public mood, extending one person's weather to a whole country.
normal.cn: 市场与报纸谈「公众情绪」，把一个人的天气扩到整个国家。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the lamp does not change but the walls seem to brighten and dim.
abstract.cn: 想象灯没有变，墙面却似乎忽明忽暗的屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that responds to conversation rather than to air.
abstract.cn: 想象一个对谈话而不是对空气作出反应的恒温器。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when the person inside feels like it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有在里面的人有兴致时才开的门。

examples.en: The mood in the office lifted as soon as the results arrived.
examples.cn: 结果一到，办公室里的气氛就轻松起来。

examples.en: I am not in the mood for a debate tonight.
examples.cn: 我今晚没兴致辩论。

examples.en: The subjunctive mood is rare in modern spoken English.
examples.cn: 虚拟语气在现代英语口语中很少见。

dict_mnemonic.text: mood 读如「木的」——人一时像木头一样闷着 → 心情、情绪、气氛

root: 两条独立来源：表感受的义项出自古英语 mod「心、勇气、性情」，属日耳曼语；表语气的语法义借自拉丁 modus「尺度、方式」，与 mode、model 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person has weather, and that weather is then read as a room's temper, as a recurring bad spell, as a manner of speaking, as a public climate, as an open door, as a pattern of swings and finally as a key chosen by an artist.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：人有天气，这天气依次被读作一间屋子的脾气、一再出现的坏脾气、一种说话方式、公众气候、一扇开着的门、一串起落的模式，最后是艺术家选定的调子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room whose lamp never changes, yet the walls seem to brighten and dim as clouds cross the roof.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯始终没变的屋子，云从屋顶走过时墙面却忽明忽暗。

branches.en: WEATHER AND ITS RECORD: one sense is a single stretch of feeling, the other the chart of how often it turns.
branches.cn: 天气与它的记录：一个是单段感受，另一个是它翻转频率的图表。

branches.en: A SPACE WITH A TEMPER: the same weather either fills a room or is deliberately composed into a work.
branches.cn: 有脾气的空间：同一种天气要么充满一间屋子，要么被刻意编进一件作品。

branches.en: THE SPELL OTHERS LEARN: a bad mood made plural becomes a recurring event in a household.
branches.cn: 旁人学会的那阵子：坏心情一旦用复数，就成了一户人家反复发生的事。

branches.en: THE OTHER HISTORY: here the word does not mean feeling at all, but the manner in which a verb speaks.
branches.cn: 另一段历史：这里这个词完全不指感受，而指动词说话的方式。

branches.en: CLIMATE AND INCLINATION: one is a whole public's weather, the other a single door that is open or shut.
branches.cn: 气候与意愿：一个是整个公众的天气，另一个是单扇开或关的门。

intro.en: The word is short and native, so the interesting structure lies in its family and in the separate Latin homograph.
intro.cn: 这个词又短又是本族语，因此有意思的结构在它的词族，以及那个同形异源的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: Only the grammar sense has Latin behind it, from modus 'measure, manner'; the feeling word has no Latin ancestry at all.
latinIntro.cn: 只有语法义背后有拉丁语，出自 modus「尺度、方式」；表感受的那个词完全没有拉丁来历。

items.example: The mood in the hall went flat.
It forms the adjective for someone given to moods.
items.exampleCN: 它构成形容某人容易闹情绪的形容词。

items.meaning: given to low or irritable states
items.meaningCN: 容易陷入低落或烦躁的
items.exampleCN: 考试前他变得闷闷不乐。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for the trait.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成该特质的名称。

items.meaning: the trait of changing mood quickly
items.exampleCN: 情绪多变在青春期很常见。

items.meaning: music chosen to create an atmosphere
items.meaningCN: 为营造气氛而选的音乐
items.example: The café plays mood music all afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆整个下午放着氛围音乐。

items.example: The doctor asked about mood swings.
items.exampleCN: 医生询问了情绪波动的情况。

items.structure: Latin modus (source of the grammar sense)
items.example: The grammar sense is a separate Latin borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 语法义是一次独立的拉丁借入。

derivatives.zh: 情绪化的；闷闷不乐的
闷闷不乐地
喜怒无常
影响情绪的

definition_zh: 陈述；声明；说法；报表；结单
definition_en: something said or written that gives information, or an official report of money or facts
core_image: 一方印着字的纸从机构窗口递出——白纸黑字，字字可查
scene: 月底，银行信件准时寄到家里。 The bank statement showed every payment she had made that month.
sceneCN: 这里 statement 是「对账单；结单」（第 4 个义项：机构出具的正式报表）；句意为银行对账单列出了她当月的每一笔支出。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「陈述；说明」
由本词加-ed 构成，义为「获正式教育评估的（英国特殊教育用语）」
由 mis- 加本词构成，义为「错误陈述」

senses.title: Something said or written that gives information
senses.definition: a sentence or set of words giving information or an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 给出信息或观点的句子或词组
senses.example: The report contains several questionable statements.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里有几处可疑的表述。
senses.why: Facts are set out in words, fixed like lines on a page.
senses.whyCN: 事实以文字陈列，如纸上固定的行列。

senses.title: An official public announcement
senses.definition: a formal announcement made to the public or press
senses.definitionCN: 面向公众或媒体的正式公告
senses.example: The company issued a statement about the safety recall.
senses.exampleCN: 公司就安全召回发布了声明。
senses.why: The institution sets its words in an official frame.
senses.whyCN: 机构把自己的话放进正式的框里。

senses.title: An expression of attitude through dress or action
senses.definition: clothes, art, or actions that declare a personal stance
senses.definitionCN: 借服装、艺术或行动宣示个人立场
senses.example: Her bright red coat was a real fashion statement.
senses.exampleCN: 她那件鲜红大衣真是一场时尚宣言。
senses.why: What you wear is read like written words.
senses.whyCN: 你的穿着如文字般被解读。

senses.title: An official report of money or facts
senses.definition: a printed record of money movements, sales, or facts over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内资金流动、销售或事实的打印记录
senses.example: Check your statement before paying the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 付账前先核对一下对账单。
senses.why: Numbers, like words, are set out in an official list.
senses.whyCN: 数字与文字一样被陈列在正式单据上。

senses.title: A formal sentence in logic or law
senses.definition: a sentence that can be judged true or false in logic, or a formal account in law
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中可判定真假的句子，或法律中的正式陈述
senses.example: In logic, every statement is either true or false.
senses.exampleCN: 在逻辑学中，每个命题非真即假。
senses.why: The sentence is fixed in a frame where truth can be tested.
senses.whyCN: 句子被固定在可检验真假的框架里。

intro.en: Statement is state plus -ment: words that are set out in a fixed, official form.
intro.cn: statement 即 state 加 -ment：以固定、正式形式陈列的话语。

items.en: The stand-root *sta- underlies state and statement.
items.cn: 「站立」词根 *sta- 是 state 与 statement 的基础。

items.en: Latin stare grew into state via Old French estat, meaning a standing condition.
items.cn: 拉丁 stare 经古法语 estat 长出 state，意为「站立的状态」。

items.en: The verb state, "to set out in words", formed in English.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语形成动词 state「以文字陈明」。

items.en: Adding -ment gave statement: the words so set out.
items.cn: 加 -ment 构成 statement：如此陈明的言语。

items.en: Bank statements, official statements, and fashion statements spread the noun widely.
items.cn: 银行结单、官方声明与时尚宣言让该名词广泛传播。

note.en: Statement grows from the stand-root family and pairs with the say-family of announcement words.
note.cn: statement 由「站立」词族长出，并与「言说」词族的公告类词配对。

entries.definition: a condition, a country, or the verb to say formally
entries.definitionCN: 状态；国家；陈述；statement 的词基

entries.definition: a wrong statement
entries.definitionCN: 错误陈述；由 mis- 加本词

entries.definition: a written law
entries.definitionCN: 成文法；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a public notice of news
entries.definitionCN: 公告；通知

entries.definition: a formal and public statement
entries.definitionCN: 宣布；宣言

entries.definition: a confident claim made without proof
entries.definitionCN: 断言；主张

entries.definition: a casual spoken comment
entries.definitionCN: 随口评论；与正式声明相对

normalIntro.en: Five real hooks for statement and its state-root.
normalIntro.cn: 五条真实钩子帮助记住 statement 及其 state 词根。

normal.en: state + -ment: the words formally set out.
normal.cn: state + -ment：正式陈明的话语。

normal.en: a bank statement: money set out line by line.
normal.cn: bank statement：资金逐行陈列。

normal.en: make a statement: clothes can talk too.
normal.cn: make a statement：衣着也会说话。

normal.en: misstatement: the wrong words were set out.
normal.cn: misstatement：陈明错了的话。

normal.en: state and statement share the old stand-root.
normal.cn: state 与 statement 共享古老的「站立」词根。

abstract.en: See a sealed envelope marked OFFICIAL STATEMENT.
abstract.cn: 看见封口盖着 OFFICIAL STATEMENT 的信封。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger page ruled with straight lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页划满直线的账册。

abstract.en: Hear a spokesperson read calm words to the cameras.
abstract.cn: 听发言人面对镜头平静宣读。

examples.en: Her statement to the police was short and clear.
examples.cn: 她对警方的陈述简短清晰。

examples.en: The painting makes a bold statement about war.
examples.cn: 这幅画对战争作出了大胆的表述。

examples.en: The monthly statement arrives by email now.
examples.cn: 月度结单如今通过电子邮件送达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯得特门特」——像「死白的门特」：白纸黑字，从门里递出的正式文书。

root: statement 由动词 state「陈明」加名词后缀 -ment 构成；state 经古法语 estat 上溯拉丁 stare「站立」，属「站立」词族。

sensesIntro.en: Statement is words set out in a fixed frame: said, published, worn, printed, or tested for truth.
sensesIntro.cn: statement 是被固定框定后陈列的话语：说出、发布、穿上、打印或接受真伪检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: words fixed into a formal frame and set out
core.cn: 核心意象：话语被固定进正式框架后陈列

branches.en: words judged by what they claim
branches.cn: 据所言内容接受评判的话语

branches.en: the institution's public words
branches.cn: 机构的公开言辞

branches.en: clothes and acts that read like words
branches.cn: 如文字般被解读的衣着与行动

branches.en: numbers set out like words
branches.cn: 如文字般陈列的数字

branches.en: the plain information sense
branches.cn: 单纯的信息义项

intro.en: Statement is state with a suffix that turns action into a thing.
intro.cn: statement 是 state 加上把动作转为名词的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare, from the stand-root, is the deep base of state and statement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare 出自「站立」词根，是 state 与 statement 的深层基础。

items.example: The minister stated her position clearly.

items.meaning: the thing produced by the action
items.example: Agreement and statement both end in -ment.
items.exampleCN: agreement 与 statement 都以 -ment 结尾。

items.example: The audit found a misstatement of costs.
items.exampleCN: 审计发现成本陈述有误。

items.meaning: given a formal record, as in education
items.example: A statemented child receives extra support.
items.exampleCN: 获正式评估的儿童可获额外支持。

items.example: Her bank statement arrived on the first.
items.exampleCN: 她的银行结单一号到达。

items.example: Oversized glasses are a fashion statement.
items.exampleCN: 超大眼镜是一种时尚宣言。

items.example: An official statement followed the accident.
items.exampleCN: 事故之后发布了官方声明。

items.example: Latin stare is the deep root of state.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 stare 是 state 的深层词根。

derivatives.zh: 由 mis- 加本词构成，义为「错误陈述」
由本词加-ed 构成，义为「获正式教育评估的」

definition_zh: 照片；相片；拍照；拍摄
definition_en: a picture made with a camera, in which light is recorded on film or a sensor; to take such a picture
core_image: 快门一响，一小片光被钉在纸上，成了可以拿在手里的画面
scene: 老式相机架在木架上，摄影师让孩子别动，等光刚好落在脸上。 She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里是「拍照」（第 2 个义项：用相机记录）；句意为她在下雨之前把整条街拍了下来。木架、黑布和等待光线的孩子都指向「按下快门」这个动作。

derivatives.zh: photograph 换 -ic 词尾，义为「摄影的；与摄影有关的」
photo- 加 -graphy，义为「摄影术」；-graphy 指书写、记录的过程，与 -graph 的成品相对
photograph 加 -er，义为「摄影师」；同一词干上 -er 专门指人
photo- 加 -genic（产生），义为「上相的；适合拍照的」

senses.title: A picture made by light
senses.definition: a picture formed when light from a scene is recorded on film or on a sensor inside a camera
senses.definitionCN: 相机把景物反射的光记录在胶片或传感器上而形成的画面
senses.example: He kept a photograph of his grandparents on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他在书桌上放着一张祖父母的照片。
senses.why: The Greek elements say light writing, so the object is literally what light wrote on a surface; English named the finished result before it named the act of making it.
senses.whyCN: 两个希腊成分合起来是「用光书写」，照片就是光在表面上写下的东西；英语先给这个成品命名，再给制作它的动作命名。

senses.title: To take a picture with a camera
senses.definition: to take a picture of a person, place or event with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用相机把人、地点或事件拍成照片
senses.example: She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 她在下雨前拍下了整条街。
senses.why: English lets a product noun become a verb with no ending at all; photograph, copy and film all travel this zero-conversion path, so noun and verb sound identical.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许指成品的名词不加词尾直接变成动词；photograph、copy、film 都走这条零转换的路，所以名词和动词读音完全相同。

senses.title: To come out in a certain way in pictures
senses.titleCN: 上相；在照片里呈现某种样子
senses.definition: to appear in photographs in a particular way, especially attractively
senses.definitionCN: 在照片里呈现出某种样子，尤指好看、上镜
senses.example: That dark blue coat photographs well in winter light.
senses.exampleCN: 那件深蓝色外套在冬日光线里很上相。
senses.why: Once the verb means to record, it can also judge the record: the subject, not the camera operator, is being assessed for how it looks on film, which is why the adverb well fits so naturally.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦表示「记录下来」，就能评判记录的效果：被评估的是被拍对象在照片里的样子，而不是拍摄者的技术，所以 well 这个副词用在这里特别自然。

intro.en: Photograph is a nineteenth-century coinage from two Greek words, and its three endings -graph, -grapher and -graphy settled into English within a few years of one another.
intro.cn: photograph 是十九世纪用两个希腊词造出来的新词；-graph、-grapher、-graphy 三种结尾在英语里几乎同时定型。

items.en: Phos, whose genitive is photos, meant light and supplied the combining form photo-.
items.cn: phos 的属格是 photos，意为光，提供了组合形式 photo-。

items.en: Graphein meant to scratch, carve, draw or write, and the noun graphe meant a drawing or a piece of writing.
items.cn: graphein 意为刻、雕、画、写，名词 graphe 指图画或文字。

items.en: French and German writers formed photographie for the new light-made image, and Sir John Herschel is usually credited with the English photograph in 1839.
items.cn: 法国和德国的作者为新出现的感光影像造出 photographie；一般认为英语的 photograph 由约翰·赫歇尔在 1839 年确定。

items.en: English fixed -graph for the image, -er for the person and -y for the practice, all on the same Greek base, which is why the family looks so regular.
items.cn: 英语用同一希腊词干固定了三种结尾：-graph 指影像，-er 指人，-y 指技艺，所以这一族词看起来格外整齐。

items.en: The verb came by conversion, and the clipped photo took over everyday speech while photograph stayed in captions, labels and technical writing.
items.cn: 动词由名词零转换而来；口语里由 photo 这个截短形式承担，photograph 则留在图注、标签和技术文字中。

note.en: The look-alike group shows how the same Greek base changes its ending for object, person, adjective and practice; the near-meaning group collects other names for a camera image.
note.cn: 形近组展示同一希腊词干如何靠不同结尾分别指物、指人、指性质、指技艺；近义组收其他表示「相机影像」的词。

entries.definition: The art or process of making photographs; -graphy names the practice, not the object.
entries.definitionCN: 拍摄照片的技艺或过程；-graphy 指做法，不指物件。

entries.definition: The person who takes photographs; -er marks the human agent.
entries.definitionCN: 拍照的人；-er 标记施动的人。

entries.definition: Relating to photography, or able to record light chemically or electronically.
entries.definitionCN: 与摄影有关的，或能以化学、电子方式记录光的。

entries.definition: A machine-made copy of a page; it borrows photo- but its second half is Latin copy, not the Greek -graph.
entries.definitionCN: 机器复制出的一页副本；借了 photo-，后半却是拉丁语 copy，不是希腊语 -graph。

entries.definition: A visual image of any kind, painted, drawn or taken with a camera.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的视觉图像，画的、绘的或拍的。

entries.definition: A visible representation, often used for what appears on a screen or in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 可见的呈现，常用于屏幕上的画面或心中的形象。

entries.definition: A quick, informal picture taken without much preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 随手拍下、不做多少准备的快照。

entries.definition: A photograph or painting of a person, usually centred on the face.
entries.definitionCN: 人物照片或画像，通常以脸为中心。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek sentence compressed into a compound, and its endings tell you whether you are holding the thing, the person or the craft.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一句希腊语压成复合词，它的结尾告诉你手里拿的是东西、是人，还是手艺。

normal.en: Photo- is light and -graph is what is written or drawn, so a photograph is light's drawing.
normal.cn: photo- 是光，-graph 是被写下、被画出的东西，所以 photograph 就是光的画。

normal.en: -graph gives the thing, -grapher gives the person, -graphy gives the practice: three endings, three jobs.
normal.cn: -graph 给出实物，-grapher 给出人，-graphy 给出技艺：三种结尾，三种分工。

normal.en: The verb photograph adds nothing to the noun; English simply uses the thing-word as an action-word.
normal.cn: 动词 photograph 没有加任何词尾；英语直接把指物的词拿来指动作。

normal.en: Photograph well judges how the subject looks in pictures, not how skilled the person holding the camera is.
normal.cn: photograph well 评判的是被拍对象在照片里的样子，不是持相机者的技术。

normal.en: In speech photo does most of the work, while photograph belongs to captions, forms and formal description.
normal.cn: 口语里多由 photo 承担，photograph 则出现在图注、表格和正式描述中。

abstract.en: A photograph is light that was stopped and taught to stay on a surface.
abstract.cn: 照片是被拦下来的光，被教会停在某个表面上。

abstract.en: The word splits the world into light and writing, which is why a good picture can feel like a sentence.
abstract.cn: 这个词把世界分成「光」与「书写」，所以一张好照片读起来像一句话。

abstract.en: Every photograph is also a decision about what was left outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每张照片同时也是一次决定：决定把什么留在画框之外。

examples.en: He kept a photograph of his grandparents on the desk.
examples.cn: 他在书桌上放着一张祖父母的照片。

examples.en: She photographed the whole street before the rain came.
examples.cn: 她在下雨前拍下了整条街。

examples.en: That dark blue coat photographs well in winter light.
examples.cn: 那件深蓝色外套在冬日光线里很上相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「否头格拉夫」——光在纸上写下的一格画面；记住 photograph 是照片，也能当动词「拍照」。

root: 希腊语 phos/photos（光）+ graphein（刻、画、写），合成「用光写下的东西」；-graph 指写下的成品，-grapher 指写的人，-graphy 指写的过程或技艺。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an image written by light; the noun names the image, the verb names the act, and the third sense judges how a subject comes out in the image.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是由光写成的画面；名词指画面，动词指拍摄动作，第三个义项则评判被拍对象在画面里呈现得如何。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shutter opening for a fraction of a second while light burns a small image onto a surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：快门只开了一瞬，光在表面上烙下一小块画面。

branches.en: a framed picture standing on a desk
branches.cn: 立在书桌上的带框照片

branches.en: a hand lifting a camera in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中举起相机的手

branches.en: a coat that looks better on film than in the room
branches.cn: 在照片里比在屋里更好看的外套

branches.en: the picture and the act that produced it
branches.cn: 照片与拍出它的那个动作

branches.en: a face kept after the person has gone
branches.cn: 人已离开却留在纸上的脸

intro.en: The compound is Greek on both sides, and English added the endings that split the family into object, person and practice.
intro.cn: 这个复合词两半都来自希腊语，英语再加上不同结尾，把这一族分成物、人和技艺。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的词根是希腊语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 操作员；接线员；运算符；经营者
definition_en: a person who works a machine, a telephone switchboard or a service, or a symbol that stands for an operation in mathematics and computing
core_image: 控制台前一个人戴着耳机，把一排闪烁的推子逐个扶正
scene: 演播室外的控制台上，一个戴耳机的年轻人盯着指示灯，把每一路声音逐一推稳。 The operator kept every channel balanced during the live broadcast.
sceneCN: 这里是「操作员」（第 1 个义项：负责操纵设备的人）；句意为直播时那位操作员让每个声道都保持平衡。图中可辨识物件：调音台推子、指示灯、耳机。

pos.zh: 操作员；接线员；运算符；经营者

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语过去分词词干加 -tion 构成，义为「操作；手术；运算」
由拉丁语 operatus 进入英语，义为「运转；操作；经营」
由 operation 加 -al 构成，义为「运作上的；可使用的」

senses.title: A person who works equipment
senses.definition: someone who controls a machine, a vehicle or a piece of equipment as their job
senses.definitionCN: 以操纵机器、车辆或设备为职业的人
senses.example: The crane operator stopped the load when the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风变大时，起重机操作员停下了吊运的货物。
senses.why: Latin operator means one who works, and English narrowed that to a person whose work is running a particular machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operator 意为「干活的人」，英语把范围收窄成「专管某一台机器的人」。

senses.title: A person on a telephone switchboard
senses.definition: someone who connects telephone calls in an office, a hotel or an exchange
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室、旅馆或交换台为用户接通电话的人
senses.example: The operator put me through to the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 接线员帮我把电话接到了经理那里。
senses.why: Early exchanges were manual, so connecting calls was real work done by hand, and the general word for a worker became the job title.
senses.whyCN: 早期电话交换全靠人工，接电话线是真用手做的活，于是「干活的人」这个泛称就成了岗位名称。

senses.title: A mathematical or logical symbol
senses.definition: a symbol that stands for an operation, such as plus, minus or AND in a program
senses.definitionCN: 表示一种运算的符号，如加号、减号，或程序中的逻辑与
senses.example: In this expression, the plus sign is an operator.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个表达式里，加号就是一个运算符。
senses.why: In mathematics and computing an operation is a defined action on values, and the mark that triggers it takes the name of the one who performs work.
senses.whyCN: 在数学与计算里，运算是对数值执行一种规定的动作，而触发这个动作的记号，就借用了「干活者」的名字。

senses.title: A company that runs a service
senses.definition: a business that runs a service such as transport, tours or a network
senses.definitionCN: 经营运输、旅游或网络等服务的公司
senses.example: The bus operator added two night routes this year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公交运营公司今年新增了两条夜班线路。
senses.why: A company that keeps a service running is, in the word's older sense, the one doing the work, so it too is called an operator.
senses.whyCN: 让一项服务持续运转的公司，按这个词的本义就是「干活的那一方」，所以它也被称作 operator。

intro.en: Operator is the Latin agent noun for a worker, taken into English with its meaning almost unchanged and then narrowed to particular jobs.
intro.cn: operator 是拉丁语里表示「干活者」的施事名词，进入英语时意思几乎没变，后来才收窄到各个具体岗位。

items.en: Operari meant to work or to have an effect, and it supplied the verb at the centre of this family.
items.cn: operari 意为干活或起作用，是这个词族的核心动词。

items.en: Operator was the agent noun: the one who works, a maker or a doer.
items.cn: operator 是施事名词：干活的人、制作者、行动者。

items.en: English adopted operator for a person who performs work, especially skilled or technical work.
items.cn: 英语借入 operator，指从事工作的人，尤指有技术含量的工作。

items.en: With the telegraph and the telephone, operator became the title of the person who connected lines by hand.
items.cn: 随着电报与电话出现，operator 成了手工接线者的岗位名称。

items.en: Modern English extends it to machine drivers, service companies and the symbols that trigger operations in mathematics.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到机器操作者、服务公司，以及数学中触发运算的符号。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin work family that operator belongs to; the near-meaning group is other words for people who run or tend equipment.
note.cn: 形近组是 operator 所属、由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是其他表示看管或摆弄设备的人的词。

entries.definition: To work, to control a machine or to perform surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 运转；操作机器；动手术。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Relating to how something works in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 与实际运作有关的。

entries.definition: Working, in force, or a person doing secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，或从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: A person trained to look after technical equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、负责技术设备的人。

entries.definition: A person who repairs and adjusts machines.
entries.definitionCN: 修理和调校机器的人。

entries.definition: A person or device that directs how something runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥某事物如何运转的人或装置。

normalIntro.en: Operator is the person-shaped member of the Latin work family, so the mnemonics follow -or, the suffix that turns work into a worker.
normalIntro.cn: operator 是拉丁语「干活」词族中「人」的那一格，联想就沿着 -or 走：这个后缀把「活」变成「干活的人」。

normal.en: Operator is operari plus -or, the doer of the work.
normal.cn: operator 是 operari 加 -or，就是「干活的那个人」。

normal.en: Operation is the work itself, so operator and operation are the doer and the deed.
normal.cn: operation 是「活」本身，operator 与 operation 正好是做事的人与所做的事。

normal.en: A telephone operator works the switchboard by hand, which is why the title survived the machines.
normal.cn: 电话接线员靠手在交换台上干活，所以这个称呼在机器时代还留了下来。

normal.en: In a program, the operator is the sign that performs the operation.
normal.cn: 在程序里，operator 就是执行那个运算的符号。

normal.en: A tour operator runs the trips, so a company, not only a person, can carry the name.
normal.cn: tour operator 负责组织行程，所以不只是人，公司也能叫这个名字。

abstract.en: One person at a console holding many channels steady: work made visible as a pair of hands.
abstract.cn: 一个人守在控制台，把许多声道扶稳：活就这样变成看得见的一双手。

abstract.en: The word for a doer quietly became a job title, then a symbol on a page.
abstract.cn: 「干活者」这个说法悄悄变成岗位名，又变成纸上的一个符号。

abstract.en: Every machine that runs well has someone, somewhere, who knows its sounds.
abstract.cn: 每台转得顺的机器背后，总有个在某个角落听懂它声音的人。

examples.en: The operator kept every channel balanced during the live broadcast.
examples.cn: 直播时那位操作员让每个声道都保持平衡。

examples.en: The operator put me through to the manager.
examples.cn: 接线员帮我把电话接到了经理那里。

examples.en: The bus operator added two night routes this year.
examples.cn: 这家公交运营公司今年新增了两条夜班线路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，跑瑞特儿」——坐在机器旁不停按按钮的那个人；记住 operator 是操作员。

root: 拉丁语 operari（干活）的施事名词 operator（干活的人）直接进入英语；同族词有 operate、operation、operational。opera 虽与它共享更远的拉丁词根，却指「歌剧」，来源路线不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person who works; the senses split into equipment, telephone lines, symbols in an expression, and companies that run a service.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「干活的人」；义项随后分成看管设备、守电话线、表达式里的符号，以及经营服务的公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a console, headset on, bringing a row of flickering sliders back into line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人戴着耳机守在控制台，把一排闪烁的推子逐个扶正。

branches.en: a crane driver watching a load swing in the wind
branches.cn: 吊车司机盯着风里晃动的货物

branches.en: hands resting on a console during a quiet shift
branches.cn: 安静的班上，双手搭在控制台上

branches.en: a voice saying which line is calling
branches.cn: 一个报出哪条线来电的声音

branches.en: a plus sign doing its work on two numbers
branches.cn: 一个加号在两个数上干活

branches.en: a timetable printed by the company that runs the buses
branches.cn: 经营公交的公司印出的时刻表

intro.en: The word is the Latin verb for working plus the agent suffix -or, and the same stem then gives the act, the adjective and the symbol.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「干活」的动词加施事后缀 -or 构成；同一词干随后又给出行为、形容词和符号的说法。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is the agent noun of the working verb, so the word has meant one who works from the start.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的拉丁语来源是「干活」动词的施事名词，所以它从一开始就是「干活的人」的意思。

items.meaning: a person who works a machine

latinEntries.meaning: to work, to produce an effect

definition_zh: 壁橱；小房间；秘密的
definition_en: a cupboard built into a wall for hanging clothes, a small private room, or kept secret
core_image: 墙内那扇不起眼的窄门，门后挂满外套
scene: 卧室墙边有一扇不显眼的窄门，门缝里露出大衣的下摆。 The coats are hanging in the closet by the door.
sceneCN: 这里 closet 指「壁橱」（第 1 个义项：嵌在墙里挂衣服的柜子）；句意是外套挂在门边的壁橱里。

derivatives.zh: 闭门不出的；秘而不宣的
一柜之量

senses.title: A built-in cupboard
senses.definition: a cupboard built into the wall of a room, used for hanging clothes
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在房间墙壁里、用来挂衣服的柜子
senses.example: She hung her winter coat in the closet.
senses.exampleCN: 她把冬衣挂进了壁橱。
senses.why: The French word named any small enclosed space, and a cupboard for clothes is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 法语原词指任何小的围合空间，而挂衣服的柜子正是这种空间。

senses.title: A small private room
senses.definition: a small room used for private talk or study
senses.definitionCN: 用来私下交谈或读书的小房间
senses.example: The two men spoke in a closet behind the library.
senses.exampleCN: 两个人在图书室后面的小房间里谈话。
senses.why: Before it meant a cupboard, the word meant a closed private room for study or prayer.
senses.whyCN: 在指柜子之前，这个词指供读书或祈祷的封闭小室。

senses.title: Kept secret
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe a hidden habit or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，形容隐藏的习惯或情感
senses.example: He is a closet poet who never shows his work.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个从不示人的秘密诗人。
senses.why: Whatever is kept in a closed room stays unseen, so the noun became an adjective for hidden things.
senses.whyCN: 关在小房间里的东西看不见，于是名词变成了形容隐藏之物的形容词。

intro.en: Closet is a small enclosure in French, built on the Latin word for shut.
intro.cn: closet 是法语里的小围合空间，建立在拉丁语表示关闭的词上。

items.en: Clausum described something shut or enclosed.
items.cn: clausum 描述关上的或围合的事物。

items.en: Closet meant a small private room.
items.cn: closet 指私人的小房间。

items.en: English used closet for a private chamber of study or prayer.
items.cn: 英语用 closet 指读书或祈祷的私室。

items.en: The sense of a cupboard for clothes became common.
items.cn: 指挂衣壁橱的含义变得常见。

items.en: The adjective sense of a hidden habit took hold.
items.cn: 表示隐藏习惯的形容词义固定下来。

items.en: Closet now means both the cupboard and the secret.
items.cn: closet 如今既指柜子，也指秘密。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words from the same shut family, while the meaning group names storage furniture.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「关闭」词族的词，近义组列出储物家具。

entries.definition: to shut something or bring it to an end
entries.definitionCN: 关闭某物或结束某事

entries.definition: the act of shutting a place or an activity
entries.definitionCN: 关闭某地或某项活动的行为

entries.definition: a covered walk in a monastery or convent
entries.definitionCN: 修道院中带顶的回廊

entries.definition: a large piece of furniture for keeping clothes
entries.definitionCN: 存放衣物的大件家具

entries.definition: a piece of furniture with doors and shelves
entries.definitionCN: 带门和搁板的家具

entries.definition: a cupboard with drawers and shelves
entries.definitionCN: 带抽屉与搁板的橱柜

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the small shut room, the clothes rail and the secret kept behind the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从关闭的小室、挂衣杆和门后的秘密入手。

normal.en: Closet is close plus -et, a small shut place.
normal.cn: closet 就是 close 加 -et，一个关起来的小地方。

normal.en: A closet is smaller than a room and larger than a box.
normal.cn: closet 比房间小，比盒子大。

normal.en: American homes say closet where British homes may say cupboard.
normal.cn: 美式住宅说 closet，英式住宅可能说 cupboard。

normal.en: Come out of the closet means step out of the closed room.
normal.cn: come out of the closet 就是走出那间关着的屋子。

normal.en: A closet poet keeps the poems behind the door.
normal.cn: closet poet 把诗藏在门后。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow door in a bedroom wall, a row of coats inside.
abstract.cn: 想象卧室墙上的一扇窄门，里面一排外套。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny study with one chair and one candle.
abstract.cn: 想象一间只有一把椅子和一支蜡烛的小书房。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook hidden on the top shelf, out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象顶层搁板上藏着一本看不见的笔记本。

examples.en: She hung the dress in the closet and shut the door.
examples.cn: 她把裙子挂进壁橱，关上了门。

examples.en: The old house has a narrow closet under the stairs.
examples.cn: 这座老房子在楼梯下有一个窄小的储物间。

examples.en: He is a closet cook who never invites anyone to dinner.
examples.cn: 他做得一手好菜，却从不请人吃饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 closet 记成「关起来的小格子」：门一合，衣服和秘密都收在里面。

root: 源自古法语 closet（小围合空间），出自拉丁语 clausum（关上的），与 close 同源。

sensesIntro.en: From a small shut room to a cupboard for clothes, then to anything kept hidden.
sensesIntro.cn: 从关闭的小室，到挂衣服的柜子，再到任何隐藏起来的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow door in a wall, closed on what lies inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的一扇窄门，把里面的东西关住。

branches.en: The cupboard sense keeps the shape of a small closed space.
branches.cn: 柜子义保留了小型封闭空间的样子。

branches.en: The room sense is the older one, kept for private talk and study.
branches.cn: 房间义更古老，用于私下交谈与读书。

branches.en: What stays behind a closed door becomes a picture of secrecy.
branches.cn: 留在关门之后的东西成了秘密的写照。

branches.en: A private room and a private habit share the same wall.
branches.cn: 私人房间与私人习惯共用同一堵墙。

branches.en: The cupboard hides coats the way the adjective hides a habit.
branches.cn: 柜子藏外套，正如同形容词藏起一种习惯。

intro.en: The stem closet takes compounds and two endings, all pointing back to a closed space.
intro.cn: 词干 closet 接受复合与两个词尾，都指回封闭空间。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin clausum, shut, which became French clos and then closet.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 clausum（关上的），后成法语 clos，再加词尾成 closet。

items.example: The flat has closets in both bedrooms.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓两间卧室都有壁橱。

items.meaning: kept private or shut away with someone
items.meaningCN: 秘而不宣的；闭门相对的
items.example: The two leaders were closeted for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 两位领导人闭门谈了一个小时。

items.meaning: as much as a closet can hold
items.example: She owns a closetful of scarves.

items.exampleCN: 他们租了一间壁橱大小的办公室。

items.meaning: the door that closes a cupboard
items.example: The closet door will not shut properly.

items.meaning: a cupboard large enough to enter
items.example: The main bedroom has a walk-in closet.
items.exampleCN: 主卧有一个可步入式衣帽间。

items.example: Old houses rarely have enough closet space.
items.exampleCN: 老房子很少有足够的储物空间。

items.meaning: an old term for a toilet room
items.example: The sign on the door said water closet.

latinEntries.exampleCN: clausum 在法语中变成 clos。

definition_zh: 雇用；使用；使忙于
definition_en: to pay someone to work for you, or to make use of something
core_image: 工厂门口，经理把工作牌递给新工人
scene: 这家工厂雇用了三百多名工人。 The factory employs more than three hundred workers.
sceneCN: 这里 employ 是「雇用」（第 1 个义项：付钱请人工作）；句意：这家工厂雇用了三百多名工人。

collocations.zh: 充分就业的；全神贯注的

derivatives.zh: 雇员
雇主
就业；雇用
失业

senses.title: To hire someone for work
senses.definition: to give someone a job and pay them for their work
senses.definitionCN: 给某人工作并为其劳动付钱
senses.example: The company employs fifty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了五十个人。
senses.why: Work is exchanged for money, so the word first names the act of taking a person into paid service.
senses.whyCN: 劳动与金钱交换，因此这个词首先指把人纳入有薪工作的行为。

senses.title: To make use of something
senses.definition: to use a method, tool, or material for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的使用方法、工具或材料
senses.example: They employ a simple method.
senses.exampleCN: 他们采用一种简单的方法。
senses.why: A tool is taken into service much as a worker is, so the hiring sense extends to using things.
senses.whyCN: 工具像工人一样被纳入使用，因此雇用义扩展到使用事物。

senses.title: To keep oneself busy
senses.definition: to keep oneself or another person occupied with an activity
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或他人忙于某项活动
senses.example: She employed herself in reading.
senses.exampleCN: 她埋头读书。
senses.why: Time and attention are put to work, so the word can describe being fully occupied.
senses.whyCN: 时间和注意力被投入工作，因此这个词也能描述全神贯注的状态。

intro.en: Employ comes from a Latin word meaning to fold in or involve, which passed through French.
intro.cn: employ 来自拉丁语中意为「卷入、包含」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Implicare means to fold in or involve.
items.cn: implicare 意为卷入、包含。

items.en: Employer develops the sense of using or engaging a person.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 发展出使用、聘用某人的含义。

items.en: English borrows employ with the sense of using or occupying.
items.cn: 英语借入 employ，表示使用或占用。

items.en: The word settles into the modern sense of hiring workers.
items.cn: 在近代早期，这个词固定为雇用工人的现代义。

items.en: Employ now covers hiring, using, and keeping busy.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employ 涵盖雇用、使用和使忙于。

note.en: Employ hires or uses; hire is the plain everyday word, and use focuses on tools.
note.cn: employ 表示雇用或使用；hire 是日常说法，use 侧重使用工具。

entries.definition: a person who is paid to work

entries.definition: a person or company that hires workers

normalIntro.en: Employ means to take someone into paid work, or to put a thing to work.
normalIntro.cn: employ 意味着把人纳入有薪工作，或让某物发挥作用。

normal.en: A factory employs many workers.
normal.cn: 工厂雇用许多工人。

normal.en: She is employed by a bank.
normal.cn: 她受雇于一家银行。

normal.en: They employ a new method.
normal.cn: 他们采用一种新方法。

normal.en: An employee works for an employer.
normal.cn: employee 为 employer 工作。

normal.en: Employment means having a paid job.
normal.cn: employment 意为拥有一份有薪工作。

abstract.en: Picture a badge passed from a manager to a new worker.
abstract.cn: 想象经理把工作牌递给新工人。

abstract.en: See a tool taken off a shelf and put to use.
abstract.cn: 想象工具从架上被取下投入使用。

abstract.en: Think of time being filled with useful work.
abstract.cn: 想象时间被有用的工作填满。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引普劳伊」——把人引进来干活；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 implicare（卷入），经古法语 employer 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word links paid work, the use of tools, and the filling of time with activity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词连接有薪工作、工具的使用，以及用活动填满时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a work badge handed to a new worker.
core.cn: 核心意象：递给新工人的工作牌。

branches.en: The base sense is hiring a person for pay.
branches.cn: 基本义是付钱雇用一个人。

branches.en: The hiring sense extends to using tools and methods.
branches.cn: 雇用义扩展到使用工具和方法。

branches.en: The same energy can occupy a person's time.
branches.cn: 同样的投入也能占据一个人的时间。

branches.en: People and tools are both taken into service.
branches.cn: 人和工具都被纳入使用。

branches.en: Using a method is a form of purposeful activity.
branches.cn: 使用方法是一种有目的的活动。

intro.en: Employ carries the Latin root plic, meaning to fold, inside a French verb shape.
intro.cn: employ 在法语动词外形里带着意为「折叠」的拉丁词根 plic。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor implicare means to fold in, and its root plic- appears in many English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁祖先 implicare 意为卷入，其词根 plic- 出现在许多英语词中。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 em- 开启 employ。

items.example: The root plic- hides inside employ.
items.exampleCN: 词根 plic- 藏在 employ 里。

Employment names the state of having work.
